valuation.net_debt_note: EV = market cap + latest borrowings. Screener's public page does not split cash out of other assets, so cash is not netted off; investments are shown separately.

dcf.method: 5-year FCFF: EBITDA - tax on EBIT - capex - change in net working capital; growth fades linearly from the starting rate to the year-5 rate; Gordon terminal value; equity = EV - borrowings.

inputs.growth_basis: median of 3-year, 5-year and TTM sales growth, capped 0-30%
inputs.capex_rule: depreciation + new sales / fixed-asset turnover (median of the last three years)

reverse_dcf.note: Constant sales growth for five years, at the base margin and the same WACC and terminal growth, that makes the DCF equal today's EV.

subsections.title: What the company actually does, in plain terms

blocks.text: Cummins India Limited ('CIL') designs, manufactures, distributes and services diesel and alternative-fuel engines from 2.8 to 100 litres, and diesel and alternative-fuelled generator sets up to 3,000 kW (3,750 kVA), plus related components and technology. [F] (SCREENER) It runs two reporting units: the Power Systems Business Unit (PSBU) and the Distribution Business Unit (DBU). [F] (AR2026 p.10) It was incorporated in 1962 and is 51.00% owned by Cummins Inc., USA. [F] (AR2026 p.123) (NUMBERS)

How it makes money, using the segment disclosure management gives on earnings calls (standalone net sales basis): in FY26 domestic power generation was **Rs 4,758 crore (+24%)**, distribution (aftermarket parts and service) **Rs 3,278 crore (+22%)**, domestic industrial **Rs 1,650 crore (-1%)**, high-horsepower exports **Rs 984 crore (+20%)** and low-horsepower exports **Rs 807 crore (+3%)**. [F] (CALL Jun 2026) Those five lines sum to Rs 11,477 crore against reported net sales of Rs 11,949.73 crore, leaving roughly Rs 473 crore (4.0%) unallocated in management's own segment build. [E] (CALL Jun 2026) (AR2026 p.230)

Annual report and call agree [F] (AR2026 p.13)

blocks.text: Geography: the company serves India, Bhutan and Nepal and exports to 86 countries, with America, Europe, Mexico, Africa, the Middle East and China named as top destinations. [F] (AR2026 p.11) (AR2026 p.123) Exports were 16.65% of turnover in FY26; revenue from contracts with customers split Rs 10,084.77 crore India and Rs 2,006.88 crore outside India. [F] (AR2026 p.123) (AR2026 p.231) By product code, internal combustion engines were 54% of turnover, engine parts and accessories 23% and generating sets 18%. [F] (AR2026 p.123)

Customer profile: end users, OEMs and channel partners (dealers, distributors, retailers), serving data centres, construction, compressors, mining, marine, railways, oil and gas, pumps, defence and power generation. [F] (AR2026 p.123) (AR2026 p.11) Sales to dealers and distributors were 16% of total sales across 179 dealers, with the top ten accounting for 72% of dealer sales. [F] (AR2026 p.136) The single most important concentration fact is buried in the consolidated segment note: **sales of approximately Rs 3,734.71 crore came from three external customers in FY26, against Rs 2,226.78 crore from two customers in FY25** - about 30.8% of consolidated revenue from operations versus 21.4% a year earlier. [F] (AR2026 p.340) [E] The customers are not named anywhere in the documents. [F] (AR2026 p.340)

Listing status: this is not a recent listing. The shares have been listed on BSE (code 500480) and NSE (CUMMINSIND) for decades, with face value reduced from Rs 100 to Rs 10 in February 1987 and from Rs 10 to Rs 2 in December 2000. [F] (AR2026 p.89) (AR2026 p.91) The evidence base is therefore a mature one - 65 annual reports, quarterly transcripts, a full audit history - and there is no IPO-prospectus information asymmetry to discount. What is missing is not history but current operating granularity: no order book, no installed capacity, no market share and no segment margins are disclosed. [F] (AR2026, searched) (CALL Aug 2026)

blocks.text: Classifying the drivers: theses 2, 3 and 8 are **structural** - installed-base economics, regulatory capability and parent technology access do not reverse with the cycle. [AI] Theses 4, 5 and 6 are **company-specific** - a debt-free, cash-heavy, low-capex configuration that is a management choice and a group treasury outcome, not an industry feature. [AI] Theses 1 and 7 are **cyclical, dressed as structural**: data-centre revenue is recognised on installation at site and depends on hyperscaler site clearances, which management itself calls 'lumpy business' [MC] (CALL Nov 2025); rail, mining, marine and defence are tender-driven and 'keeps changing quarter to quarter' [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). [AI]

subsections.title: The bear case: ten reasons not to own it

items: **1. The price does not intersect any scenario in our model.** Our DCF produces Rs 448.9 per share in the bear case, Rs 757.6 in the base case and Rs 1,039.7 in the bull case, against a market price of Rs 5,100; the reverse DCF says the price requires a 78.1% sales CAGR for five years versus a 13.0% base-case equivalent. [F] (NUMBERS) Even the most generous corner of the sensitivity grid - a 13.5% WACC with 6.5% terminal growth - gives Rs 996. [F] (NUMBERS)

**2. Growth has concentrated into one lumpy end-market and three unnamed customers.** Three external customers produced about Rs 3,734.71 crore of FY26 consolidated sales, up from two customers at Rs 2,226.78 crore - roughly 30.8% of revenue versus 21.4%. [F] (AR2026 p.340) [E] Data centres moved from 23% to 40% of quarterly power-generation revenue in a year. [F] (CALL Aug 2026) The annual report explicitly warns the data-centre business 'is characterised by variability aligned with timing of large project executions and customer commitments'. [F] (AR2026 p.51)

**3. The margin has already turned, and the pricing response lags.** Q1 FY27 operating margin was 18%, against 21-22% in each of the prior four quarters, and PAT rose just 0.8% on sales up 17.9%. [F] (NUMBERS) Management took no price increase in Q1 and one at the start of Q2, with 'price realization will start happening a few months down the line because we do run backlogs', and conceded 'will we be able to recover all commodity increases through this price rise? No.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

**4. Strip out data centres and the core power-generation business grew about 5%.** On the disclosed Q1 FY27 mix, non-data-centre power generation grew in the low single digits; management did not dispute the framing, attributed it to 'a little bit of supply constraint', and refused to comment on market share. [E] [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) Management has consistently said it has no syndicated market-share data at all. [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) (CALL Feb 2026)

**5. Related-party dependence is large, rising, and about to be authorised at nearly the size of the company.** 52% of purchases and 17% of sales are with related parties. [F] (AR2026 p.136) FY26 actual transactions with the four material related parties were about Rs 5,985 crore; the FY27 caps put to shareholders total Rs 10,591 crore - roughly 87% of FY26 consolidated turnover. [F] (AR2026 p.392) (AR2026 p.393) (AR2026 p.394) [E] Prices are set by internally applied cost-plus formulas (cost plus at least 11% on engines and gensets sold, cost plus 14% on components), arm's-length tested 'internally by the management', with 'A copy of the valuation or other external party report' marked 'Not applicable'. [F] (AR2026 p.401) (AR2026 p.400)

**6. Charges from the parent are growing several times faster than sales.** Support services paid to Cummins Inc. rose to Rs 213.01 crore from Rs 102.93 crore (+107%), royalty to Rs 77.94 crore from Rs 70.65 crore, and reimbursements paid to Cummins Technologies India to Rs 295.20 crore from Rs 137.74 crore (+114%), against sales growth of 17%. [F] (AR2026 p.245) Royalty and support services together were about 2.4% of FY26 net sales versus about 1.7% in FY25. [E] Management explained the royalty move as standardisation of rates that 'used to range between 1% to 8%' down to a single 4%. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) The FY27 proposal adds a Rs 118.77 crore 'Transfer of Technology' line to Cummins Inc. [F] (AR2026 p.398)

**7. Cash conversion has lagged profit for years, and got worse.** Operating cash flow was 0.73x PAT in FY26, 0.77x over three years and 0.76x over five. [F] (NUMBERS) Working capital absorbed Rs 503 crore in FY26 against Rs 72 crore in FY25, led by a Rs 460 crore increase in receivables. [F] (AR2026 p.278) The cash conversion cycle widened to 60 days from 49. [F] (NUMBERS)

**8. About a quarter of pre-tax profit does not come from selling engines.** Consolidated other income was Rs 517.34 crore (interest Rs 188.50 crore, rent Rs 186.13 crore, investment gains Rs 74.84 crore, miscellaneous Rs 67.87 crore) plus an equity-accounted share of joint venture and associate profit of Rs 266.28 crore. [F] (AR2026 p.318) (AR2026 p.276) On our statements data this appears as an 'other income' line of Rs 702 crore, 22.7% of PBT. [F] (NUMBERS)

**9. Contingent liabilities tripled in one year.** Total contingent liabilities rose to Rs 303.16 crore from Rs 98.80 crore, driven by GST matters at Rs 234.50 crore versus Rs 4.33 crore - principally a Rs 229.74 crore disallowance of input tax credit and additional output tax demand for FY20 to FY22, pending before the Additional Commissioner. [F] (AR2026 p.238) (AR2026 p.187)

**10. Disclosure stops exactly where an investor needs it, and leadership is in flux.** No order book, no backlog, no installed capacity, no market share, no segment margins and no quantum for the price increase are disclosed anywhere in the documents. [F] (AR2026, searched) (CALL Aug 2026) The 78-litre and 95-litre engines that the market will need if data-centre sites scale are not made in India. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) On the Q1 FY27 call an analyst wished the Managing Director well 'post your departure' and management confirmed only that 'Cummins management is involved and they are absolutely looking to appoint a rightful successor for me'. [F] [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) The company has had three Chief Financial Officers between January 2025 and July 2025. [F] (AR2026 p.254)

subsections.title: Key debates: where the market may be wrong, in both directions

blocks.caption: Five live debates
columns: The case the consensus may be missing
rows: Is data-centre demand a structural platform or a project cycle?
India's data-centre build-out is early and multi-year; inquiry momentum 'continues, very strong' and now covers 'the next year and the year after that' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Revenue is recognised only as gensets are installed at site, order-to-install is 6-12 months, and management calls the hyperscaler portion lumpy and dependent on site clearances [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) (CALL Nov 2025). The Q3 FY26 power-gen decline of 16% YoY was caused purely by data-centre execution landing in the prior quarter [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)
Both are true. The demand is real; the quarterly revenue line is not a run-rate. A single quarter of slipped site clearances can turn +35% into -16%, as it already has [AI]
Is the margin peak behind or ahead?
Management says 'definitely, there is scope to improve our margins here on' and points to cost control and value engineering [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Management itself attributed the 20-quarter-high Q3 FY26 gross margin to 'some onetime supplier benefits' and product mix, both described as 'not repeatable' [MC] (CALL Feb 2026); Q1 FY27 operating margin is already 18% [F] (NUMBERS); the DCF base case assumes a 20% EBITDA margin, above the latest quarter [F] (NUMBERS)
The FY26 margin was flattered. The honest base case is that 20-21% is the ceiling of a good cycle, not a floor [AI]
Does the localisation advantage narrow as data-centre node sizes rise?
CIL's fully localised QSK60 gives it a cost edge over importing competitors [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

Management: 'the India market is still largely QSK60... In the near-term, which is 2 years, it will continue to be Q60'; but if the market shifts to 78L and 95L, 'no one is making 95 liters in India. Everybody is importing them' - and CIL would import too [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). It has not yet reached the point where it would establish 78L or 95L capacity [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)
The localisation edge is real today and conditional beyond two years. If the node mix shifts up, CIL competes on service and brand, not cost - which is exactly what management already argues [AI]
Does distribution get a CPCB IV+ aftermarket step-up?
Two-year warranties on the CPCB IV+ fleet start expiring, handing a technologically complex fleet to the only channel equipped for it [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)

Management flagged the counter-risk itself: the unorganised channel learns, and 'over time, as they learn, some of this market share could start going away'; the step-up 'will likely come 27 onwards' [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). The annual report also warns that low utilisation of standby gensets 'structurally moderates aftermarket intensity per asset' [F] (AR2026 p.54)
The step-up is probable but smaller and later than the narrative implies, and the company has refused to size it [AI]
Is the reverse DCF's 78% growth requirement a real market expectation?
The number is read as proof of extreme overvaluation [E] (NUMBERS)

78.1% annual sales growth for five years is not a coherent market expectation for a capital-goods company; it is the mechanical output of a model with a 15% WACC, 5.5% terminal growth, an EBITDA-only free cash flow definition that excludes Rs 517 crore of other income and Rs 266 crore of equity-accounted profit, and an equity bridge that deducts borrowings without adding Rs 3,925 crore of cash and liquid investments [F] (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.274) [AI]
The correct inference is not '78% growth is priced in' but 'this DCF framework cannot reconcile this price at all' - which is itself the finding. The gap is overstated but nowhere near closable [AI]

blocks.text: The market is buying a data-centre infrastructure proxy with a 40% ROCE and no debt, and is paying 59.7x trailing earnings and 54.6x EV/EBITDA for it. [F] (NUMBERS) Our variant view is narrower and less dramatic than the reverse DCF suggests: the durable, high-quality part of this company is the Rs 3,278 crore distribution annuity and the emission-compliance franchise behind it, which together compound at roughly the rate of the Indian installed base and are almost impossible to dislodge. [F] (CALL Jun 2026) [AI] The part the market is capitalising most aggressively - domestic high-horsepower power generation sold to three unnamed customers, recognised on site installation, at 40% of a quarter's power-gen revenue - is the part with the least visibility, the fewest disclosed contracts, the shortest demonstrated history and the most volatile quarterly print. [F] (AR2026 p.340) (CALL Aug 2026) [AI] Meanwhile the two things that would most change the earnings power - what proportion of value added is retained in India versus billed away as royalty, support services and related-party cost-plus margins, and whether the 18% Q1 margin is a blip or the new base - are both disclosed only in aggregate and both moved against minority shareholders in FY26. [F] (AR2026 p.245) (NUMBERS) [AI] A rational owner of this stock is underwriting a decade of high-teens compounding plus a permanent, generous group-level relationship; the evidence supports the first proposition more strongly than the second. [AI]

blocks.text: Two observations. First, the group's reported profit contains Rs 266.28 crore of equity-accounted profit from a joint venture and an associate that CIL does not control, against which cash dividends of Rs 216.75 crore were actually received (Rs 117.00 crore from CGTIPL and Rs 99.75 crore from VCPL). [F] (AR2026 p.276) (AR2026 p.245) The carrying value of these holdings is Rs 602.09 crore, 5.3% of consolidated total assets, against attributable net worth of Rs 176.88 crore for VCPL and Rs 425.21 crore for CGTIPL. [F] (AR2026 p.274) (AR2026 p.45) [E] Second, the associate is where copper cost sits: management said 'the alternator business does get hugely impacted by copper' and described the situation as 'a difficult challenge at this point in time for our associate company'. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) A commodity shock therefore hits CIL twice - through its own bill of materials and through the equity-accounted line. [AI]

The formal consolidated segment note reports only two segments, 'Engines' and 'Lubes', with Lubes being the equity-accounted joint venture and fully eliminated. [F] (AR2026 p.340) That means the granular power-generation, distribution, industrial and export split that the entire investment case rests on exists **only in earnings-call commentary**, is not audited, is not reconciled to the financial statements, and leaves a roughly Rs 473 crore FY26 residual unexplained. [F] (AR2026 p.340) (CALL Jun 2026) [E]

The corporate shell is 64 years old, but the earnings engine that the market is capitalising is about three years old. [AI] Three things all happened inside the FY24-FY27 window: the CPCB IV+ emission transition (July 2023 to July 2024), which reset the entire domestic genset product range and pricing base [MC] (CALL Feb 2026); the arrival of data centres as a major buyer, with inquiry velocity that management dates specifically to 'after October last year', meaning October 2025 [MC] (CALL Jun 2026); and a step-change in reported profitability, with operating margin moving from 14% in FY22 to 21% in FY26 and ROCE from 21% to 40%. [F] (NUMBERS) Sales grew at a 22.7% CAGR over five years but only 10.1% over nine. [F] (NUMBERS)

The leadership that delivered that step-change is also new and is changing again: the Managing Director took office on 1 September 2024 and her departure was discussed on the Q1 FY27 call without a named successor; the CFO seat changed hands three times between January and July 2025; the Chairperson has been in place since November 2023; and two of ten directors joined in August 2025 while two left in mid-2025. [F] (AR2026 p.64) (AR2026 p.254) (AR2026 p.37) (AR2026 p.38) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) An investor is therefore underwriting a three-year-old earnings profile, delivered by a two-year-old executive team, of which the leader is leaving. [AI]

sections.title: The production and service chain, and where the value actually sticks

items: **Step 1 - Technology and design.** Product platforms, emissions architecture and advanced engineering come from Cummins Inc.; CIL's own R&D spend is Rs 10.54 crore, 0.09% of sales, of which Rs 5.89 crore is capitalised. [F] (AR2026 p.34) Local engineering is described as 'analysis-led product development', simulation and validation rather than clean-sheet design. [F] (AR2026 p.22) A royalty of 4% of eligible sales and a 'Transfer of Technology' charge are paid to the parent. [F] (AR2026 p.401) (AR2026 p.398)

**Step 2 - Component and sub-assembly sourcing.** 52% of total purchases are from related parties. [F] (AR2026 p.136) The two largest are Tata Cummins Private Limited (Rs 1,399.01 crore of goods, a 50:50 Cummins-Tata Motors joint venture) and Cummins Technologies India Private Limited (Rs 1,317.31 crore, a fellow subsidiary that makes turbochargers, components and engines). [F] (AR2026 p.248) (AR2026 p.391) Alternators come from the 48.74% associate CGTIPL. [F] (AR2026 p.30) Only 1% of purchases are from trading houses, across 23 trading houses. [F] (AR2026 p.135)

**Step 3 - Engine manufacture.** Engines are built at the Kothrud Engine Plant in Pune and at Phaltan; the Kothrud plant won an Aatmanirbhar Factory Award. [F] (AR2026 p.31) (AR2026 p.14) Management confirms the Indian data-centre volume is 'still largely QSK60', which is localised, while the 95-litre engine is imported. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

**Step 4 - Genset packaging and test.** Gensets are assembled at the Power Generation Plant, Phaltan and the Pirangut Power System Plant, Pune; the genset test facility was upgraded with advanced safety standards and integrated controls in FY26. [F] (AR2026 p.31) (AR2026 p.23) 26,000+ gensets were delivered across India in FY26. [F] (AR2026 p.17)

**Step 5 - Route to market.** Three routes run in parallel: direct to large end customers and hyperscalers, where 'even before they start floating their requests, we work with them' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026); through Genset OEM (GOEM) dealers, of which there are 133, plus 14 newly onboarded '2S' dealers for the low-kVA segment [F] (AR2026 p.56); and through OEMs for industrial engines (construction, mining, marine, rail, pumps, oil and gas). [F] (AR2026 p.54) Sales to dealers and distributors are 16% of total sales. [F] (AR2026 p.136)

**Step 6 - Installation and revenue recognition.** For data centres, 'As we install the gensets on the site, we recognize the revenue'. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) Contract liabilities (customer advances) stood at Rs 121.91 crore against Rs 79.63 crore. [F] (AR2026 p.230) Installation services are treated as a distinct performance obligation. [F] (AR2026 p.236)

**Step 7 - Warranty and inspection.** Every product carries a two-year comprehensive warranty with an optional five-year extended warranty. [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) The warranty provision is Rs 129.82 crore and the New Engine Performance Inspection provision Rs 39.82 crore. [F] (AR2026 p.240) (AR2026 p.241)

**Step 8 - Aftermarket annuity.** DBU services the installed base through 480+ 4S touchpoints, 110+ retail touchpoints, one parts distribution centre and, with dealers, 3,500 trained engineers across 450 touchpoints; 877,569 service orders were executed in FY26. [F] (AR2026 p.10) (AR2026 p.18) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) Comprehensive-contract revenue on a data-centre asset 'start[s] coming after warranty period gets over, which is 2 years after installation'. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

**Step 9 - Rebuild, repower and retrofit.** A remanufacturing facility at Phaltan runs a five-stage process (disassembly, cleaning, inspection, salvage or reuse, final assembly and testing); the K50 G3 rebuild engine received a Product Carbon Footprint certification; FY26 included the first CPCB IV+ DA set order to repower non-compliant railway Power Cars, replacing other manufacturers' engines. [F] (AR2026 p.138) (AR2026 p.20) (AR2026 p.19)

subsections.title: Where value is captured, and why

blocks.text: Value is captured at two points and leaks at two others. [AI] It is captured, first, in **application engineering and certification**: the CPCB IV+ transition forced a redesign of the entire sub-800 kW range, and management reports pricing has 'largely sustain[ed] at the levels we have' after that transition, with the earlier price step described by an analyst as 30-35% and not contradicted. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) Second, and more durably, it is captured in **service density**: a promise that an engineer reaches a hospital within two hours and any other customer within four hours in a country of India's spread is not replicable by a price-led competitor, and it is what converts a one-time genset sale into a multi-decade parts-and-service relationship. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) [AI]

Value leaks, first, into the **related-party supply chain**: 52% of purchases pass through group entities at internally determined cost-plus prices, and the FY27 authorisation raises the ceiling for Cummins Technologies India alone to Rs 4,092.99 crore, 34.25% of prior-year consolidated turnover. [F] (AR2026 p.136) (AR2026 p.394) (AR2026 p.395) When asked directly whether rising CTIPL purchases would dilute margin because 'the value addition is getting divided between CTIL and Cummins India', management answered that it manufactures 'in CIL what we can' and elsewhere where there is scale, and said 'do not read anything more into it'. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) That is an assertion, not evidence. [AI] Second, value leaks into **parent charges**: royalty plus support services rose to about 2.4% of net sales from about 1.7%, and FY27 proposals imply a further increase. [E] (AR2026 p.245) (AR2026 p.398)

Outsourcing and capital intensity: this is an assembler and service network wrapped around a machining core, not a vertically integrated manufacturer. [AI] Net operating fixed assets are only Rs 1,320.88 crore of property, plant and equipment plus Rs 77.40 crore of capital work in progress and Rs 46.88 crore of right-of-use assets - 12.8% of consolidated total assets - against Rs 12,143.19 crore of revenue. [F] (AR2026 p.274) (AR2026 p.276) [E] Capex has run at 2.0-3.1% of sales for the last four years, and management states there is 'no major capital expenditure plan'. [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) The company is therefore capital-light on fixed assets and capital-heavy on working capital and idle liquidity: receivables plus inventories plus other current assets are 37.0% of the balance sheet and cash plus investments another 34.7%. [E] (AR2026 p.274)

blocks.text: **Genuinely differentiated:** high-horsepower data-centre solutions, where the moat is not the engine but the wrap - pre-tender site engineering, lead-time management, commissioning and a 99.99% uptime service commitment. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) (CALL Aug 2026) Rail and marine products, where approvals, customisation and Indian Railways or Navy qualification are the barrier. [F] (AR2026 p.15) And the aftermarket, where the CPCB IV+ fleet is 'technologically far more advanced... All engines are electronic. There is after-treatment system... a lot of telematics and sensors', which raises the capability floor for a servicer. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)

**Commodity-like, or becoming so:** the low and medium horsepower CPCB IV+ genset range, where management describes competition as 'very, very high... specifically in the low horsepower and the medium-range segment but very broad-based' with 10 to 12 players, and expects 'even higher competitive intensity also in the low horsepower range'. [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) On-highway aftermarket parts, where the annual report itself warns of 'increasing adoption of lower-cost will-fit parts and the introduction of OEM second-line brands' pressuring price and share of wallet. [F] (AR2026 p.54) And, prospectively, the very top of the range: if the data-centre node mix shifts to 78L and 95L, every competitor imports, and CIL's localisation cost advantage on the QSK60 disappears as a differentiator. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) [AI]

The uncomfortable arithmetic: the two product families the market is paying the most for - data-centre HHP and aftermarket - are also the two for which the company discloses no margin at all. Management was asked directly for 'some color on how do gross margins vary between power gen and industrial' and replied 'No, Mohit. I won't be able to give you that split.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) Any mix-driven margin thesis in this name is therefore unfalsifiable on current disclosure. [AI]

subsections.title: Power generation domestic: the data-centre engine

blocks.text: **What happened.** FY26 Rs 4,758 crore, +24%; Q1 FY27 Rs 1,424 crore, +35% YoY and +10% QoQ. [F] (CALL Jun 2026) (CALL Aug 2026) The within-quarter mix for Q1 FY27 was low horsepower Rs 77 crore, medium Rs 248 crore, heavy duty Rs 125 crore, with the remainder - about Rs 974 crore - in high horsepower. [F] (CALL Aug 2026) [E] Data centres were 40% of overall power-generation revenue, versus 23% in Q1 FY26. [F] (CALL Aug 2026)

**Management's explanation [MC].** 'There was some data center project execution in this particular quarter'; demand is strong across 'manufacturing, data centers, residential, commercial realty'; the non-data-centre volume growth 'has scope to grow'; and the gap between data-centre and non-data-centre growth is 'a function of' 'a little bit of supply constraint that we faced'. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) Management also confirmed prior-quarter swings were execution-timing driven: the 16% YoY decline in Q3 FY26 was 'the only difference... data center execution, which happened in the quarter before, not in this one'. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)

**Our read [AI].** On the disclosed shares, data-centre revenue roughly doubled year on year while the rest of domestic power generation grew in the low single digits. [E] (CALL Aug 2026) That is the single most important fact in this report and it cuts two ways. Positively, CIL is winning the only part of the Indian genset market that is growing fast, and it is winning it with an incumbency (pre-tender engineering, 99.99% uptime service) that a price-led entrant cannot easily copy. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) [AI] Negatively, a 40%-of-segment exposure to a business that is recognised on site installation, depends on third-party site clearances, has already produced a -16% YoY quarter, and whose customers are three unnamed parties, is not the profile of a diversified capital-goods compounder. [F] (AR2026 p.340) (CALL Feb 2026) [AI] Management's own framing supports this: 'these are all big gensets. So they take time for delivery'; hyperscaler orders 'are not very well spread out'. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) (CALL Nov 2025)

Two management statements on the data-centre share of FY26 power-generation revenue are not reconciled. On the February 2026 call: 'data center contribution overall for our business stays around 25% of the Power Gen revenue. That's on an average.' [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) On the May 2026 call: 'for the full year, the data center business would have contributed between 30% to 35% of our overall power generation domestic revenue, and for the quarter, approximately 35%.' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) Both may be internally consistent if Q4 was exceptionally data-centre heavy, but as stated they conflict and neither was corrected. We show both. [AI]

**Distribution.** FY26 Rs 3,278 crore, +22%; Q1 FY27 Rs 886 crore, +14%. [F] (CALL Jun 2026) (CALL Aug 2026) Management attributes the FY26 growth to a rising installed asset base, deeper penetration, service contracts, rebuilding its own engines, retrofit emission devices and dual-fuel kits, and says explicitly that 'Price-led growth is in the distribution business is very less'. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) On the Q1 deceleration: 'you should not read too much into 1 quarter... we had a higher base earlier. And... supply disruption sometimes cause us to deal with lower parts availability. DBU business absolutely has the potential to grow at 20% growth over this year and the next few years as well.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) Our read: this is the highest-quality revenue in the company and the explanation is credible, but a volume-led 22% grower decelerating to 14% on 'parts availability' deserves one more quarter of evidence before it is dismissed, particularly because the annual report itself warns that 'the low utilization profile of standby applications structurally moderates aftermarket intensity per asset'. [F] (AR2026 p.54) [AI]

**Industrial domestic.** FY26 Rs 1,650 crore, down 1%; Q1 FY27 Rs 458 crore, +10% YoY and +20% QoQ, split construction Rs 148 crore, rail Rs 145 crore, compressor Rs 52 crore, marine Rs 50 crore, with about Rs 63 crore across mining, defence and others. [F] (CALL Aug 2026) [E] Management's FY26 explanation: construction fell because road construction is 'at half the rate of what it was in the previous year' and an October monsoon delayed excavator offtake; mining tenders from Coal India did not come; compressors entered a cyclical downcycle; rail and marine were the offsets. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) (CALL Jun 2026) (CALL Nov 2025) Our read: the segment is genuinely tender-driven and the FY26 decline is explained rather than explained away - but it also means the 'India infrastructure' leg of the bull case has produced nothing for two years. [AI] Rail is now the largest contributor to domestic Industrial revenue, which concentrates this segment on a single monopsony buyer whose network is already 99% electrified. [F] (AR2026 p.57) (AR2026 p.51) The annual report's own threat section concedes that electrification 'is expected to limit diesel engine deployment to niche applications'. [F] (AR2026 p.54)

**Exports.** FY26 Rs 1,989 crore, +12%, of which HHP Rs 984 crore (+20%) and LHP Rs 807 crore (+3%). [F] (AR2026 p.13) (CALL Jun 2026) Q1 FY27 Rs 521 crore, flat YoY, with LHP down 20%. [F] (CALL Aug 2026) Management: growth came from Europe and Asia Pacific; 'the West Asia crisis is actually leading to some of our exports not going to the Middle East as anticipated'; and crucially, that demand is not deferred - 'whatever we are not able to fulfill the market in the Gulf will try and fulfill with whatever availability they have from their own region. These orders do not stay that long.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) Management has repeatedly declined to guide exports: 'Could I share with you that for the next 5 years, we will be able to get double-digit growth? No, because these are not the end markets that we understand as well as the India market.' [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) Our read: exports are a mix-and-currency business with no franchise, and management says so. [AI] The Euro Stage V certification and the Chile 500 kVA entry are real capability additions but too small to change the line. [F] (AR2026 p.33) [AI]

**Order-driven versus organic.** Order and tender-driven: rail, marine, mining, defence, and the hyperscaler portion of data centres. [F] (AR2026 p.15) [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) Broadly organic and continuous: distribution, the colocation portion of data centres ('The orders that we get from our local colo players are largely very well spread out'), the CPCB IV+ dealer channel, and construction and compressor engines that follow OEM build rates. [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) Export is neither - it is channel inventory and distributor-led, with 'inventory correction in our channel space' an annual event. [MC] (CALL Nov 2025)

items: **Q1 FY27 actuals.** Standalone net sales Rs 3,375 crore, +18% YoY and +14% QoQ; domestic Rs 2,854 crore, +22%; exports Rs 521 crore, flat. [F] (CALL Aug 2026) On our statements data (which includes other operating revenue), consolidated sales were Rs 3,426 crore, EBITDA Rs 616 crore, operating margin 18%, PAT Rs 609 crore and EPS Rs 21.98. **Profit did not follow revenue.** Profit before tax before exceptional items was Rs 721 crore, down 0.7% year on year and down 12% sequentially, on record revenue. [F] (CALL Aug 2026) Consolidated PAT rose 0.8% on sales up 17.9%. [F] (NUMBERS)

**Why, per management [MC].** 'higher commodity costs and inflation remain key factors influencing margins during the quarter'; steel, pig iron, aluminium and copper increases; the West Asia crisis; labour shortages at suppliers; rising freight. On employee cost specifically: the annual merit increase effective 1 April 2026, a variable-compensation true-up, and the absence of an actuarial credit booked in the prior quarter - and management confirmed the higher employee-cost base persists for the rest of the year. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

**Pricing.** No price increase was taken in Q1; one was taken at the start of Q2. The quantum was refused: 'No, it will not be possible for me to share that information.' Realisation lags 'at least a quarter' because of power-generation backlogs, and 'will we be able to recover all commodity increases through this price rise? No.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

**Deferred or postponed orders.** Management states the opposite of postponement on data centres: 'we actually have not seen that. And quite the opposite, where all the data center customers are wanting us to prepone our deliveries to them.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) On Gulf exports, unfulfilled demand is lost, not deferred. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

**Known headwinds already flagged for the rest of FY27.** Monsoon slowdown in construction 'is now anticipated'; no new national highway construction tenders; compressors in a cyclical downcycle; Middle East exports weak. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) (CALL Jun 2026)

**Known guidance.** 'The company expects moderate growth across segments in the financial year 2026/27', given at the FY26 results call; no numeric revenue or margin guidance was given for FY27 on the Q1 call. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) (CALL Aug 2026) Distribution is said to have 'the potential to grow at 20% growth over this year and the next few years'. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

**What we have deliberately not done.** We have not annualised Q1 FY27, and we have not projected FY27 revenue. No order book, backlog or booked-revenue figure is disclosed anywhere in these documents, so a bottom-up FY27 build would be invention. [F] (AR2026, searched) [AI]

[F] (AR2026 p.11) The annual report attributes FY26 export growth to low-horsepower demand in Africa, the Middle East and Europe and high-horsepower demand in Europe, Latin America, Asia Pacific and China. subsections.title: Overall read on the client base

blocks.text: Three distinct client economies sit inside one company and they have very different qualities. [AI] The **group economy** - Cummins Limited UK, CTIPL, TCPL and Cummins Inc. - is the most certain and the least controlled: it is 52% of purchases, 17% of sales, priced on internally applied cost-plus formulas, and authorised annually at levels well above actual use. [F] (AR2026 p.136) (AR2026 p.401) (AR2026 p.394) Minority shareholders have no vote on the formulas, only on the caps. [AI] The **regulated-buyer economy** - Indian Railways, the Navy, shipyards, defence OEMs - is the most defensible on approvals and the weakest on price, and the company says so itself. [F] (AR2026 p.53) The **data-centre economy** is the most valuable and the least documented: it is now the largest growth driver, it is concentrated in three unnamed customers at 31% of revenue, and the only contractual evidence in the public record is the phrase 'large orders for multiple hyperscale datacentres'. [F] (AR2026 p.340) (AR2026 p.17) [AI]

Wallet-share upside is real in exactly one place: the aftermarket. The logic is mechanical rather than promotional - every genset installed today becomes a service annuity in two years, management has a 450-touchpoint network and a 90% NPS to convert it with, and the CPCB IV+ fleet is technically harder for the unorganised channel to service. [F] (AR2026 p.18) [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) (CALL Aug 2026) What an investor cannot do from these documents is size it, because neither the installed base, nor the attach rate, nor the aftermarket margin is disclosed. [F] [AI]

sections.title: Deep dives on the three lines that decide the thesis

blocks.text: **Where CIL sits in the value chain.** CIL is the packager and lifetime servicer of standby generating sets for data-centre sites, not a developer, EPC contractor or power supplier. The saleable unit is a genset of 2,500 kVA and above, built around the QSK60 engine (localised in India) or, for larger nodes, the QSK78 and QSK95 (imported from Cummins group plants). [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) (CALL Jun 2026) The engine itself is partly sourced from the group, the alternator from the 48.74% associate, and the packaging, test, installation, commissioning and lifetime service are CIL's. [F] (AR2026 p.30) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

**What exists today versus narrative.** Exists today: data centres at 40% of Q1 FY27 power-generation revenue and 30-35% of FY26 domestic power-generation revenue [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) (CALL Jun 2026); 'about INR250 crores of value' of hyperscaler revenue in Q4 FY26 [MC] (CALL Jun 2026); 'continued execution of large orders for multiple hyperscale datacentres coming up in India' [F] (AR2026 p.17); a QSK60 G34/G37 launch in September 2026 [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS); and customers 'wanting us to prepone our deliveries'. subsections.title: Deep dive 2 - Distribution: the annuity that justifies the quality label

blocks.text: **Where CIL sits.** DBU owns the relationship with the installed base across every end market - power generation, railways, mining, marine, defence, construction and on-highway - selling parts, service contracts, rebuilds, repowers, retrofit emission devices, dual-fuel kits and, newly, energy storage and telematics. [F] (AR2026 p.55) (AR2026 p.56) [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) It is a distribution and labour business bolted onto a manufacturing company, and it is explicitly not an export business: 'Distribution business exists to serve the assets on the ground in the market... We do not really look at this business for heavy export opportunities.' [MC] (CALL Nov 2025)

**What exists today.** Rs 3,278 crore of FY26 revenue, 27.4% of net sales, up 22% [F] (CALL Jun 2026) [E]; 877,569 service orders; a 90% Net Promoter Score described as the highest ever achieved globally in the Cummins group; 480+ 4S touchpoints, 110+ retail touchpoints and one parts distribution centre; 3,500 trained engineers and 450 touchpoints including dealers; a two-hour response guarantee for critical customers such as hospitals and four hours for others; 179 dealers and distributors; approximately 10 new on-highway aftermarket product categories launched; and a remanufacturing facility at Phaltan running a five-stage rebuild process. [F] (AR2026 p.18) (AR2026 p.10) (AR2026 p.136) (AR2026 p.56) (AR2026 p.138) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

**What is narrative.** The margin. Every industry logic says aftermarket parts and service carry a materially higher gross margin than new equipment, and the board notes in this dashboard assert that 'Aftermarket parts pricing is genuinely strong'. [BOARD] But the company has never disclosed a distribution margin, refused a power-gen versus industrial gross-margin split, and the only quantified statement is negative for the pricing thesis: 'Price-led growth is in the distribution business is very less.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) (CALL Jun 2026) Also narrative: the CPCB IV+ aftermarket step-up, which management dates to 'It will likely come 27 onwards' and has never sized; and the data-centre aftermarket, which management said it 'will not be able to quantify... fully today'. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) (CALL Jun 2026)

**The company's own three warnings on this business, which the bull narrative omits.** 'the low utilization profile of standby applications structurally moderates aftermarket intensity per asset, potentially tempering revenue growth relative to base expansion'; 'Rail electrification is expected to limit diesel engine deployment to niche applications... which may reduce the overall maintenance intensity of the installed base'; and 'Intensifying competition in the on-highway aftermarket, driven by the increasing adoption of lower-cost will-fit parts and the introduction of OEM second-line brands, may exert pressure on pricing and impact share of wallet for genuine parts.' [F] (AR2026 p.54) These are the company's words, in its own threats section, and they argue that installed-base growth converts to aftermarket revenue at a decaying rate. [AI]

**Strategic implications.** This is where the durable value is, and it is also where disclosure is weakest. [AI] A 22% grower at 27% of sales with 90% NPS and a 450-touchpoint moat is the asset an investor should want to pay for; a 14% quarter attributed to 'parts availability' is the first data point that the compounding is not automatic. [F] [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) The single highest-value disclosure improvement management could make is a distribution segment margin and an installed-base attach rate. Until it does, the aftermarket quality argument in this stock rests on inference. [AI]

items: **As lessee.** Leases are for office premises, with terms between 12 and 120 months and lock-in periods between 24 and 108 months, both renewable and non-renewable. **As lessor - and this is the more interesting exposure.** The company leases out investment properties (office premises and plants) on terms of 36 to 60 months. [F] (AR2026 p.239) The contracted ladder of future minimum lease rentals receivable is Rs 46.44 crore within one year, Rs 26.64 crore in years 1-2, Rs 11.30 crore in years 2-3, Rs 1.25 crore in years 3-4 and **nil beyond year four**, a total of Rs 85.63 crore against Rs 87.38 crore a year earlier. **Why that matters.** Rent income in FY26 was Rs 186.13 crore, of which Rs 154.33 crore came from investment properties. [F] (AR2026 p.318) (AR2026 p.216) Against an annual run-rate of roughly Rs 186 crore, the total contracted minimum receivable over all future years is Rs 85.63 crore - less than six months of the income line. [E] The implication is that most of this income sits on cancellable or short-cycle arrangements that must be renewed, and it is not a bond-like annuity. [AI] Rent income is about 7.2% of FY26 EBITDA on our statements data. [E] (NUMBERS)

**Related-party leases.** The related-party note records 'Services rendered' to Cummins Technologies India of Rs 225.26 crore and to Valvoline Cummins of Rs 86.79 crore, and states that services rendered 'include renting services, testing services, business support services, etc.' [F] (AR2026 p.248) (AR2026 p.252) The rent and services components are not separated, and the FY27 related-party approvals explicitly contemplate 'rent received/paid' with Tata Cummins and Cummins Technologies India. [F] (AR2026 p.397) **Investors therefore cannot tell how much of the Rs 186 crore rent line and the Rs 1,485.52 crore fair value of investment properties is a third-party property business and how much is intra-group accommodation.** That is a real disclosure gap on an asset worth 8% of the balance sheet. We are working towards that, but we do not have a local product yet.' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

**The bigger dependence is intra-group rather than cross-border.** 52% of total purchases are from related parties, versus 51% a year earlier, and only 1% from trading houses. [F] (AR2026 p.136) (AR2026 p.135) The two largest are Tata Cummins at Rs 1,399.01 crore and Cummins Technologies India at Rs 1,317.31 crore of goods. [F] (AR2026 p.248) For components and spares bought from CTIPL for distribution, the disclosed pricing basis is 'Cost plus 5% markup'; for engines for manufacturing, 'Cost plus 11% markup'; for turbochargers, components and spares for manufacturing, 'third party pricing'. [F] (AR2026 p.401)

Supply-chain mitigation disclosed: 'Dual sourcing adjusted payment terms with financially weaker suppliers, price revisions, long term supplier agreements, inventory building (areas wherever necessary)'. [F] (AR2026 p.59) Notably, 25 Quality Control Orders were onboarded onto an internal Bureau of Indian Standards compliance tool, which is a regulatory constraint on supplier substitution. [F] (AR2026 p.21)

[AI] The FY26 accounts show the successful end of that cycle; Q1 FY27 shows the beginning of the next one. [F] (NUMBERS)

blocks.text: The gearing is severe: **every 1% move in net material cost moves EBITDA by about 3.0% and PAT by about 2.5%.** [E] Because management has confirmed that price recovery lags by at least a quarter and is incomplete, a two-quarter commodity spike of the kind described as 'unprecedented' is sufficient on its own to hold PAT flat on double-digit revenue growth - which is exactly what Q1 FY27 delivered, with PAT up 0.8% on sales up 17.9%. blocks.caption: What moved each year's margin, and whether it was structural

Temporary operating leverage becoming structural as scale rebuilt [AI]

Coincides with the CPCB IV+ transition window (July 2023 to July 2024), which management describes as resetting the entire sub-800 kW product range with content addition and, per an unrebutted analyst statement, price increases of 30-35% [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) (CALL Jun 2026); sales +15.8% and fixed-asset turnover 3.49x to 3.91x [F] (NUMBERS)
**Largely structural** - a regulatory content-and-price reset that also removed weaker competitors' product availability, plus genuine operating leverage on an unchanged asset base [AI]
Sales +15.5% with margin held; management attributes gross-margin work to 'a lot of effort... working with our suppliers on our material costs' [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) [F] (NUMBERS)
Structural on material cost programmes; no one-offs disclosed for the full year [AI]

Three identified drivers. (a) Volume and mix: data centres rose to 30-35% of domestic power generation, and Q3 FY26 gross margin reached about 38%, a 20-quarter high [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) (CALL Feb 2026). (b) **One-time supplier benefits**, which management explicitly labelled 'not repeatable' along with mix [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). (c) **Employee cost fell 0.4% on sales up 17%** with permanent headcount flat at 3,088, and a Rs 94.20 crore labour-code charge was moved below the line as exceptional [F] (AR2026 p.276) (AR2026 p.110) (AR2026 p.262)

**Mixed and flattered.** The material-cost programme is structural; the supplier one-offs, the mix and the labour-cost restraint are not. A Rs 50 crore one-time true-up of management cost charges also ran through Q3 FY26 other expenses [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) [AI]

Commodity inflation in steel, pig iron, aluminium and copper; freight increases; supplier labour shortages; the West Asia crisis; the annual merit increase effective 1 April 2026; a variable-compensation true-up; and the absence of a prior-quarter actuarial credit - with **no price increase taken in the quarter** [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

**Temporary in management's framing, but the cost base is permanently higher.** Management confirmed the higher employee-cost base persists for the rest of FY27, and the labour codes have permanently raised gratuity obligations - the defined benefit obligation rose from Rs 277.51 crore to Rs 344.37 crore including Rs 83.38 crore of past service cost from a plan amendment [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) [F] (AR2026 p.243) [AI]

blocks.text: Part of the margin improvement is structural and should persist: the CPCB IV+ content and price reset, a multi-year material-cost programme run with suppliers, and operating leverage on an asset base that has barely grown. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) [F] (NUMBERS) [AI] That accounts for most of the move from 16% in FY23 to about 20% in FY24-FY25. [AI]

The final 100 basis points in FY26 is not durable on the company's own account: management identified one-time supplier benefits and non-repeatable mix as contributors to the record Q3 gross margin, a Rs 50 crore one-time true-up ran through other expenses, and employee cost was held flat on a 17% revenue increase while the labour-code cost step-up was classified as exceptional rather than operating. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) [F] (AR2026 p.262) [AI] Q1 FY27 has already given back three percentage points. [F] (NUMBERS)

**Our conclusion: treat 20% as the mid-cycle EBITDA margin and 18% as the current run-rate, not 21% as the new floor.** [AI] Management's own guidance language supports the caution - asked twice whether gross margins would return to historic levels, the answer was 'I will not be able to say whether we will hit historic highs or not, because these are unprecedented times' and 'in a 2-year time frame, I may not be able to give you an answer of where the gross margins will land'. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) The one unambiguous commitment is directional only: 'definitely, there is scope to improve our margins here on.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) Note also that the annual report's own key-ratio table reports an 'Operating Profit Margin' of 28.9% for both FY26 and FY25 on a basis the report does not define; it is not comparable with the 21% and 20% EBITDA margins in our statements data, and the two are not reconciled. [F] (AR2026 p.60) (NUMBERS) [AI]

sections.title: Unit economics: what can and cannot be built from the disclosures

subsections.title: What is and is not available

items: **Available:** number of gensets delivered in India in FY26 (26,000+) [F] (AR2026 p.17); engines and generator sets exported (5,022 and 6,369) [F] (AR2026 p.34); total service orders (877,569) [F] (AR2026 p.18); domestic power generation, distribution, industrial and export revenue [F] (CALL Jun 2026); company-wide material, employee and other cost ratios [F] (AR2026 p.276); and the within-quarter power-generation split by node for four quarters [F] (CALL Aug 2026).

**Not available, and therefore not modelled:** installed capacity in any unit; realisation per node (low, medium, heavy-duty, high horsepower); segment or product gross margins, explicitly refused [MC] (CALL Aug 2026); the installed base of gensets under service; the aftermarket attach rate; revenue per installed asset; the value of any single order; the quantum of the Q2 FY27 price increase [MC] (CALL Aug 2026); and the split between volume and price in revenue growth, described as 'very tough to do' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).
The consequence: a blended, order-of-magnitude unit economic can be built, but a per-node contribution model - which is what would be needed to underwrite a mix-driven margin thesis - cannot. [AI]

blocks.text: **Four reasons these numbers must not be used for per-node analysis.** (1) The 26,000+ figure is gensets 'delivered' across India, which need not equal revenue-recognised units in the same period, and management recognises data-centre revenue only on installation at site. [F] (AR2026 p.17) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) (2) Domestic power generation revenue spans nodes from small commercial gensets to 3,750 kVA data-centre units, so a single average conflates products whose prices differ by two orders of magnitude - the Q1 FY27 split alone shows Rs 77 crore of low horsepower against about Rs 974 crore of high horsepower. [F] (CALL Aug 2026) [E] (3) The material ratio is company-wide and includes industrial engines, exports and traded goods, not power generation alone. [E] (4) A 'service order' is an undefined unit that could be a single part sale or a full engine rebuild. [AI]

subsections.title: What would have to be true for unit economics to improve

items: **Node mix moves up.** Q1 FY27 already shows high horsepower at roughly Rs 974 crore of Rs 1,424 crore of domestic power generation, so mix is already working in this direction; the question is whether high horsepower actually carries a better contribution, which the company will not confirm. [E] (CALL Aug 2026) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

**Price recovery exceeds input inflation for two consecutive quarters.** The Q2 FY27 increase is in the market but not quantified, realisation lags at least a quarter, and management has said recovery will be incomplete. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

**Localisation deepens at the top of the range.** If 78-litre volumes justify Indian manufacture, imported content and the associated margin leakage to group plants would fall - but the decision has not been taken. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

**Aftermarket attach rate rises as the CPCB IV+ fleet leaves warranty from FY27.** This is the single largest identified lever on blended contribution, because aftermarket revenue requires no new genset to be built. Management dates it to 'likely come 27 onwards' and has never sized it. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)

**Material-cost programmes continue to deliver.** Management cites cross-functional cost reduction delivering 'substantial savings in direct material, indirect material, manufacturing overhead costs and warranty costs' and value engineering as a lever equal in importance to price. [F] (AR2026 p.22) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)
**Utilisation rises without commensurate cost.** At 70-75% there is headroom, but Q1 FY27 demonstrated that record volume and falling margin can coexist. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) [F] (NUMBERS)

**Conversely, the three things that would degrade unit economics** are a permanent step-up in parent charges (already visible: royalty plus support services from about 1.7% to about 2.4% of net sales) [E] (AR2026 p.245); a shift of value-add to group entities under cost-plus pricing [F] (AR2026 p.401) [AI]; and price competition in the low and medium horsepower range, which the annual report says is intensifying. [F] (AR2026 p.53)

sections.title: Reading the statements like a forensic analyst

blocks.text: Our statements data is screener.in's consolidated series: ten years of annuals plus a trailing twelve months, twelve quarters, ratios and shareholding. [F] (NUMBERS) It is a derived dataset, not the audited statements, and three of its conventions matter. First, 'other income' is a residual from profit before tax, so it bundles the equity-accounted share of joint venture and associate profit and absorbs exceptional items - the Rs 702 crore FY26 figure reconciles as Rs 517.34 crore of true other income plus Rs 266.28 crore of equity-method profit less the Rs 81.61 crore exceptional charge. [E] (AR2026 p.276) (AR2026 p.318) Second, 'fixed assets' of Rs 2,383 crore includes Rs 906.68 crore of investment property leased out for rent. [E] (AR2026 p.274) Third, enterprise value is computed as market capitalisation plus borrowings with **no netting of cash**, which the data itself flags. [F] (NUMBERS) The audited statements in the annual report are standalone and consolidated for FY26 and FY25 only; earlier years are not available in this folder, so gross margin, working-capital components and expense composition can only be built for those two years. [F] The report prints the full statements separately; figures below are quoted with years rather than reproduced in full. [AI]

items: **Revenue quality is good but not pristine.** Revenue from operations of Rs 12,143.19 crore includes Rs 193.46 crore of other operating revenue: scrap sales Rs 7.04 crore, export incentives Rs 51.54 crore and 'others' Rs 134.88 crore comprising testing income, engineering income and royalty income from dealers. [F] (AR2026 p.230) Net sales - the number management quotes on calls - are Rs 11,949.73 crore. Both circulate as 'revenue' in the same annual report. [AI]

**Revenue recognition is the single key audit matter**, specifically because 'The Company uses a variety of shipment terms with customers, and this has an impact on the timing of revenue recognition' and because transaction price 'often includes elements of variable consideration such as discounts and incentives'. [F] (AR2026 p.176) The auditor tested revenue recorded around the year-end date and examined journal entries on risk-based criteria. [F] (AR2026 p.177) Rs 11,330.84 crore of revenue was recognised at a point in time and Rs 760.81 crore over time. [F] (AR2026 p.231)

**Other income is large and increasingly non-operating.** Consolidated other income was Rs 517.34 crore: interest Rs 188.50 crore, rent Rs 186.13 crore, gains on redemption of investments Rs 74.84 crore and miscellaneous Rs 67.87 crore. [F] (AR2026 p.318) Add the Rs 266.28 crore equity-accounted share and non-operating income was Rs 783.62 crore against profit before tax of Rs 3,085.95 crore - 25.4%. [E] (AR2026 p.276) In our statements data the equivalent line is 22.7% of PBT, down from 44.4% in FY21 but still material. [F] (NUMBERS)

**Employee cost behaved oddly and will normalise upward.** Consolidated employee benefits expense fell 0.4% to Rs 794.68 crore while revenue rose 17%, with permanent headcount flat at 3,088. [F] (AR2026 p.276) (AR2026 p.110) The explanation is visible in the exceptional item: the Rs 94.20 crore labour-code charge and Rs 83.38 crore of gratuity past service cost were taken below the operating line. [F] (AR2026 p.262) (AR2026 p.243) Management has confirmed the employee-cost base steps up from Q1 FY27 and stays higher. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

**Exceptional-item classification flatters the guided metric.** Management guides and reports on 'profit before tax before exceptional items', which was Rs 3,104.44 crore. [F] (AR2026 p.192) (CALL Jun 2026) The Rs 94.20 crore labour-code charge is genuinely regulatory and one-off in timing, but it reflects a permanent increase in employee obligations, and excluding it from the guided metric while the higher run-rate cost flows through future operating lines is presentationally favourable. [F] (AR2026 p.262) [AI]

**Tax is unremarkable.** Effective tax was 23.7% on standalone profit before tax (Rs 724.21 crore on Rs 3,054.39 crore) with Rs 12.56 crore of tax for earlier years; the ten-year effective rate has sat at 22-23% every year except FY19 (31%) and FY20 (13%). [E] (AR2026 p.192) (NUMBERS)

**No share-based payment cost sits in CIL's equity.** The company has no stock option scheme of its own; the Managing Director's Rs 7.33 crore package includes 'stock options of Holding Company', and Rs 14.38 crore was credited to other equity as 'Equity contribution from Cummins Inc. share based payments'. [F] (AR2026 p.77) (AR2026 p.197) The cost is recognised but funded by the parent - a common-control feature that slightly understates the economic cost of employing the team versus a standalone peer. [AI]

**It is not really an industrial balance sheet.** Consolidated total assets of Rs 11,304.21 crore comprise cash, deposits and investments Rs 3,925.20 crore (34.7%), working-capital assets Rs 4,184.08 crore (37.0%), operating fixed assets and capital work in progress Rs 1,445.16 crore (12.8%), investment property Rs 906.68 crore (8.0%), equity-method investments Rs 602.09 crore (5.3%), intangibles and intangibles under development Rs 129.23 crore (1.1%) and other assets Rs 111.77 crore (1.0%). [E] (AR2026 p.274)

**Liabilities are minimal.** No borrowings at either year end; lease liabilities Rs 36.51 crore; trade payables Rs 1,649.98 crore including Rs 92.66 crore to micro and small enterprises; provisions Rs 392.75 crore; deferred tax liability Rs 96.07 crore. Current ratio 3.32 against 3.12. [F] (AR2026 p.275) (AR2026 p.60) (AR2026 p.342)

**Equity is Rs 8,475.16 crore, book value Rs 306 per share**, of which Rs 1,142.02 crore is a general reserve and Rs 59.92 crore an accumulated equity contribution from the parent for share-based payments. [F] (AR2026 p.275) (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.197)

**Investment property is carried well below fair value.** Net block Rs 906.68 crore against a registered-valuer fair value of Rs 1,485.52 crore, generating Rs 154.33 crore of rental income and Rs 100.36 crore of profit before indirect expenses. [F] (AR2026 p.216) The valuation uses a discounted cash flow method with estimated rents of Rs 32.45 to Rs 138 per square foot per month and a 13.80% discount rate. [F] (AR2026 p.217)

**Receivable quality improved even as days rose.** Trade receivables Rs 2,754.27 crore, of which Rs 480.45 crore from related parties; expected credit loss provision 0.30% against 0.43%; credit-impaired receivables Rs 8.20 crore against Rs 9.77 crore; and undisputed receivables more than six months past due fell to about Rs 38 crore from about Rs 84 crore. [F] (AR2026 p.221) [E] Rs 67.24 crore is due from firms or companies in which a director is a partner, director or member, up from Rs 19.99 crore - a 3.4x increase that is disclosed but not explained. [F] (AR2026 p.221) [AI]

**Inventory is clean.** Rs 1,168.45 crore with only Rs 1.43 crore written down to net realisable value; goods in transit Rs 181.25 crore within raw materials; inventory turnover 7.00x against 6.73x. [F] (AR2026 p.218) (AR2026 p.60) CARO confirms physical verification at reasonable intervals with discrepancies below 10% for each class. [F] (AR2026 p.184)

**Investments are conservative.** Rs 1,548.43 crore of current investments, of which Rs 1,359.87 crore in liquid and money-market mutual funds and Rs 188.56 crore in quoted bonds of PFC, REC, SIDBI, HDFC Bank and NABARD. [F] (AR2026 p.219) (AR2026 p.220) Disclosed price sensitivity is Rs 6.80 crore on a 0.50% move. [F] (AR2026 p.346) There is no equity-market or credit-risk exposure of consequence. [AI]

**Operating cash flow was Rs 1,734.26 crore against Rs 2,361.75 crore of consolidated PAT - a ratio of 0.73x**, and against Rs 1,682.59 crore in FY25, growth of just 3.1% while PAT grew 18%. [F] (AR2026 p.278) (NUMBERS)

**The gap is working capital, not profit quality.** Cash generated before working capital and tax was Rs 2,863.57 crore; working-capital changes consumed Rs 503.09 crore (against Rs 72.11 crore in FY25) and tax Rs 626.22 crore. [E] (AR2026 p.278) Within working capital, receivables absorbed Rs 460.10 crore and inventories Rs 146.21 crore, partly offset by payables and other liabilities. [F] (AR2026 p.278)

**Investing cash flow was positive Rs 14.99 crore** because Rs 2,340.16 crore of term deposits were withdrawn and only Rs 1,937.67 crore reinvested, funding a Rs 542.68 crore net increase in short-term investments and Rs 251.71 crore of capex. [E] (AR2026 p.278) In other words, FY26's reported investing inflow is a treasury reshuffle, not asset monetisation. [AI]

**Financing cash flow was negative Rs 1,495.05 crore, of which Rs 1,483.02 crore was dividends.** [F] (AR2026 p.279) Free cash flow in our statements data was Rs 1,487 crore - almost exactly the dividend. [F] (NUMBERS) [E] The company is distributing essentially all of its free cash flow, which is consistent with a 77% payout ratio and with having no reinvestment need. [F] (NUMBERS) [AI]

**Over three years the company generated Rs 3,955 crore of free cash flow and over five years Rs 5,402 crore**, with cumulative operating cash flow at 0.77x and 0.76x PAT respectively. [F] (NUMBERS) The persistence of a sub-1.0x ratio through a period of strong growth is the defensible reading - a company growing revenue at 16-23% will structurally absorb working capital - but it also means reported earnings overstate distributable cash by roughly a quarter. [AI]

**Non-cash items worth noting:** Rs 266.28 crore of equity-accounted profit is added back in full (cash dividends of Rs 216.75 crore are shown in investing) [F] (AR2026 p.278); Rs 14.38 crore of parent-funded share-based payment is added back [F] (AR2026 p.278); and additions to right-of-use assets are explicitly non-cash investing activities. [F] (AR2026 p.238)

sections.title: Working capital: eleven days worse, and eight of them are self-inflicted

blocks.text: The headline is that the cash conversion cycle widened from 49 days to 60 and working capital days from 46 to 53. [F] (NUMBERS) Taken alone that reads as deterioration. Two things make it misleading. First, the working-capital days measure nets a Rs 3,925 crore liquidity pile against operating liabilities, so it tells you little about operating discipline in a company with no debt. [E] (AR2026 p.274) [AI] Second, and more important, **the deterioration is mostly a payables decision, not a receivables failure**: of the 11-day increase in the cash conversion cycle, 8 days came from paying suppliers faster and only 3 from slower collection, with inventory days unchanged. [E] (NUMBERS)

blocks.caption: Working-capital component build (balances consolidated, Rs crore; days from our statements data)
rows: Of which micro and small enterprises

blocks.text: Balances are from the consolidated balance sheet and the payables and receivables notes; days and the decomposition are from our statements data and our arithmetic. [F] (AR2026 p.274) (AR2026 p.275) (AR2026 p.221) (AR2026 p.229) (NUMBERS) [E] Note that revenue grew 16.9% while receivables grew 20.9% and inventories 16.4% - receivables grew faster than sales, inventories broadly in line. [E]

items: **The payables compression is disclosed and deliberate.** The annual report lists among its supply-chain resilience measures 'Dual sourcing adjusted payment terms with financially weaker suppliers, price revisions, long term supplier agreements, inventory building'. [F] (AR2026 p.59) The hard evidence is in the MSMED note: payments made to micro and small suppliers beyond the appointed day fell from Rs 481.64 crore in FY25 to Rs 75.96 crore in FY26, an 84% reduction, while the MSME payable balance rose 35.6% to Rs 92.66 crore. [F] (AR2026 p.231) [E] Interest paid under Section 16 of the MSMED Act was Rs 0.24 crore against Rs 0.57 crore and nothing remains accrued and unpaid. [F] (AR2026 p.231) This is a company that materially improved its payment behaviour to small suppliers - a governance positive that mechanically worsened its cash conversion cycle. [AI]

**Receivable days rose but receivable quality improved.** Undisputed receivables more than six months past due fell to about Rs 38 crore from about Rs 84 crore; the expected credit loss rate fell to 0.30% from 0.43%; credit-impaired receivables fell to Rs 8.20 crore from Rs 9.77 crore; and there is a Rs 450.91 crore secured balance. [F] (AR2026 p.221) [E] Terms are 30 to 90 days. [F] (AR2026 p.221) The increase is a growth and mix effect - larger project invoices with installation-linked milestones - not a collection problem. [AI]

**Management has not been asked about, and has not volunteered, an explanation for the working-capital increase on any of the four calls.** Searching the transcripts, working capital, receivable days and cash conversion are never discussed. [F] (CALL Nov 2025) (CALL Feb 2026) (CALL Jun 2026) (CALL Aug 2026) The only adjacent comment is on supply disruption causing 'lower parts availability' in distribution. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) **This is a gap in the analyst dialogue as much as in the disclosure.** [AI]

**Contract liabilities rose 53% to Rs 121.91 crore**, which is a mild positive - more customer money held before delivery - and is consistent with data-centre projects being pre-funded in part. [F] (AR2026 p.230) [AI]

**One item deserves a question.** Trade and other receivables due from firms or private companies in which a director is a partner, director or member rose to Rs 67.24 crore from Rs 19.99 crore. [F] (AR2026 p.221) The amount is small (2.4% of receivables) and the most likely counterparty is Tata Cummins, where the Managing Director is a non-executive director, but the report does not name it. [E] [AI]

blocks.text: **Consequence.** Working capital consumed Rs 503.09 crore of cash in FY26 against Rs 72.11 crore in FY25, which is the entire reason operating cash flow grew 3.1% while profit grew 18%, and the reason CFO/PAT fell to 0.73x. [E] (AR2026 p.278) (NUMBERS) Free cash flow of Rs 1,487 crore still covered the Rs 1,483.02 crore dividend almost exactly, so the balance sheet did not deteriorate - cash rose from Rs 234.99 crore to Rs 500.01 crore and total liquid assets rose. [F] (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.279) (AR2026 p.274) [E] The right way to state the risk is not that cash conversion is broken but that **at the current payout ratio of 77% there is no longer a cushion between free cash flow and the dividend**: another year of similar working-capital absorption with slower profit growth would have to be met from the treasury rather than from operations. [E] (NUMBERS) [AI]

**Covenants and bank limits.** The company has 'been sanctioned working capital limits in excess of Rs. 5 crores, in aggregate, from banks on the basis of security of current assets', and has filed quarterly returns with those banks that 'are in agreement with the unaudited books of account' - a clean CARO statement, with no discrepancy between bank returns and books, which is one of the more common places forensic problems surface. [F] (AR2026 p.184) The limit amount, utilisation and any covenants are not disclosed, but with nil borrowings at both year ends and interest on borrowings of Rs 0.02 crore for the year, covenant risk is immaterial. [F] (AR2026 p.234) (AR2026 p.342) [AI] Bankers are State Bank of India, HDFC Bank, Citibank, Bank of America, ICICI Bank, HSBC and J.P. Morgan Chase. [F] (AR2026 p.28)

blocks.text: **The contingent-liability trebling deserves more attention than it received.** Contingent liabilities rose from Rs 98.80 crore to Rs 303.16 crore, driven almost entirely by a Rs 229.74 crore GST input-tax-credit disallowance for FY20 to FY22. [F] (AR2026 p.324) (AR2026 p.187) The amount equals 9.7% of FY26 consolidated PAT and 3.6% of equity. [E] Management's position is that 'its position will likely be upheld in the appeal process', and no provision has been made. [F] (AR2026 p.324) The item was not mentioned on any of the four earnings calls and no analyst asked about it. [F] [AI]

**Related-party leases.** No related-party lease is separately quantified. The FY27 related-party approvals explicitly contemplate 'rent received/paid' and 'lease of business asset(s) and/or equipment(s)' with Tata Cummins and Cummins Technologies India, and the related-party note states that services rendered 'include renting services'. [F] (AR2026 p.397) (AR2026 p.252) Given that investment properties comprise 'office premises and plants' and generate Rs 154.33 crore of rent, the absence of a related-party versus third-party split on an Rs 906.68 crore asset with a Rs 1,485.52 crore fair value is a genuine gap. [F] (AR2026 p.216) [AI]

**Solvency: outstanding.** Nil debt, interest cover of 258x, a current ratio of 3.32, Rs 3,925 crore of liquid assets against Rs 150.66 crore of capital commitments, an unqualified auditor statement that nothing suggests any material uncertainty about meeting liabilities falling due within a year, no cash losses in FY26 or FY25, and no wilful-defaulter status. [F] (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.274) (AR2026 p.189) On solvency alone this is a 9 or 10 out of 10 balance sheet. [AI]

**Composition: middling, and that is what the ROCE does not show.** Only 12.8% of assets are the manufacturing base that earns the 40% return; 34.7% sits in mutual funds, bank deposits and PSU bonds earning Rs 188.50 crore of interest, which on Rs 3,925 crore of average-ish balances is a pre-tax yield in the high single digits at best; and a further 8.0% sits in rental real estate earning Rs 100.36 crore before indirect costs. [E] (AR2026 p.274) (AR2026 p.318) (AR2026 p.216) A shareholder therefore owns a superb 40%-ROCE operating business plus a large, low-return treasury and property portfolio bolted on. [AI] With a 77% payout ratio and a stated absence of major capex plans, the obvious question - never asked on any of the four calls - is what the Rs 3,925 crore is for. [F] [AI]

**Contingency: deteriorating but manageable.** The contingent-liability trebling, the unquantified provident-fund exposure and the acknowledged undisclosed litigation together represent real but bounded risk against Rs 8,475 crore of equity and Rs 3,925 crore of liquidity. [E] (AR2026 p.324) (AR2026 p.274) **Overall we would characterise balance-sheet quality as high, with the reservation that a third of it is not working.** [AI]
