subsections.title: CARO observations and the three items that matter

items: **Clean on the usual danger points.** Proper records of property, plant and equipment and intangibles; phased physical verification over two years with no material discrepancies; title deeds held in the company's name; no revaluation; no benami proceedings; inventory verified at reasonable intervals with discrepancies below 10% per class; **quarterly returns filed with banks agree with the unaudited books**; no loans, advances in the nature of loans, guarantees or security given to any party; no deposits accepted; cost records maintained; regular in depositing undisputed statutory dues; no unrecorded transactions surrendered in tax assessments; no borrowings and not a wilful defaulter; no short-term funds used for long-term purposes; no funds taken to meet the obligations of the associate or joint venture; no IPO, FPO, preferential allotment or private placement; related-party transactions in compliance with Sections 177 and 188; internal audit system commensurate with size and its reports considered; no non-cash transactions with directors; no cash losses in FY26 or FY25; no material uncertainty about meeting liabilities falling due within a year; and CSR unspent amounts on ongoing projects transferred to a special account. [F] (AR2026 p.184) (AR2026 p.185) (AR2026 p.188) (AR2026 p.189)

**Item 1 - the audit-trail exception, stated inside the opinion paragraph.** 'In our opinion, proper books of account as required by law have been kept by the Company so far as it appears from our examination of those books, **except that the backup of audit trail (edit log) maintained in electronic mode has not been maintained on a daily basis on servers physically located in India during the period April 01, 2025 to May 17, 2025**'. [F] (AR2026 p.179) Separately the auditor confirms the audit-trail feature itself operated throughout the year with no instance of tampering, and prior-year trails have been preserved. [F] (AR2026 p.181) Our read: a 47-day data-residency lapse in backup, not a control failure or an integrity issue - but it is a qualification-in-substance on books of account, it is the second consecutive year the Indian audit profession has been reporting these, and it is the kind of item that should be closed and disclosed as closed. [AI]

**Item 2 - whistle-blower investigations ongoing at the date of the audit report.** 'the Company has received whistle-blower complaints during the year, which have been considered by us for any bearing on our audit... As explained by the management, there were certain complaints in respect of which investigations are ongoing as on the date of our report and our consideration of the complaints having any bearing on our audit is based on the information furnished to us by the management.' [F] (AR2026 p.188) The number, subject matter and outcome are not disclosed anywhere, the Directors' Report describes the vigil mechanism without reference to these complaints, and no analyst raised it on any call. [F] (AR2026 p.36) [AI] This is the single most open-ended accounting-quality item in the report. [AI]

**Item 3 - the disputed statutory dues schedule, which is long and getting longer.** Roughly Rs 308 crore of disputed dues across income tax (Rs 55.89 crore spanning AY2006-07 to AY2022-23), sales tax and VAT, entry tax, service tax and CENVAT, customs (Rs 8.90 crore for FY18 to FY22 on 'Incorrect availment of concessional customs duty benefits') and GST (Rs 231.86 crore, dominated by the Rs 229.74 crore input-tax-credit disallowance for FY20 to FY22). [E] (AR2026 p.186) (AR2026 p.187) Some matters date to FY1999-2000 and sit in the Bombay High Court. [F] (AR2026 p.186) The oldest items are trivial; the GST item is not. [AI]

**Exceptional-item presentation.** The Rs 94.20 crore labour-code charge and the Rs 44.15 crore standalone (Rs 12.59 crore consolidated) gain on the subsidiary sale are both shown below the operating line. [F] (AR2026 p.262) The labour-code charge includes Rs 83.38 crore of gratuity past service cost from a plan amendment - a permanent increase in obligation, not a cash one-off - and management's headline metric is 'profit before tax before exceptional items'. [F] (AR2026 p.243) (CALL Jun 2026) The accounting is permissible and clearly disclosed; the presentational effect flatters the guided metric. [AI]

**Common-control accounting - parent-funded share-based payments.** Rs 14.38 crore (FY25: Rs 15.23 crore) is credited to a separate 'Equity contribution from Cummins Inc. share based payments' reserve, now Rs 59.92 crore cumulatively, for a scheme 'managed and administered by the Holding Company'. [F] (AR2026 p.197) CIL itself has no stock option scheme. [F] (AR2026 p.77) The employee cost is recognised, but the dilution and the funding sit with the parent. [AI]

**The Rs 31.56 crore difference in the gain on the subsidiary sale** between standalone (Rs 44.15 crore) and consolidated (Rs 12.59 crore) books reflects the elimination of previously consolidated results and is properly explained. [F] (AR2026 p.45) [AI]

**Provisioning looks measured rather than aggressive in either direction.** Warranty provision rose to Rs 129.82 crore on additions of Rs 106.34 crore and utilisation of Rs 95.41 crore - so the provision is building slightly faster than claims, consistent with a growing and more complex CPCB IV+ fleet. [F] (AR2026 p.240) The New Engine Performance Inspection provision fell to Rs 39.82 crore on additions of only Rs 5.35 crore against utilisation of Rs 15.88 crore, a Rs 14.50 crore release in substance that is not explained. [E] (AR2026 p.241) [AI] The statutory-matters provision was reduced by Rs 2.75 crore. [F] (AR2026 p.241)

**Revenue judgements are disclosed with unusual clarity**, including the treatment of bundled equipment and installation as distinct performance obligations, the use of most-likely-amount and expected-value methods for volume rebates, and an explicit statement that variable consideration estimates are not constrained. [F] (AR2026 p.236)

**Fair-value judgement on investment property** uses a discounted cash flow with a 13.80% discount rate, rents of Rs 32.45 to Rs 138 per square foot per month and rent growth of 3-15% every three years, by a registered valuer. [F] (AR2026 p.217) The property is carried at cost less depreciation, so the Rs 578.84 crore of unrecognised appreciation is disclosed but not booked - conservative. [E] (AR2026 p.216)

blocks.text: **Overall accounting-quality assessment: above average for an Indian listed industrial, with narrow but real reservations.** The positives are substantive: unmodified opinions, a single narrow key audit matter, no goodwill, no capitalised cost games, bank returns agreeing with books, no fraud, no restatement, no related-party loans or guarantees, clean fixed-asset and inventory verification, conservative investment-property carrying value, and a Big-Four auditor now reappointed under a fresh five-year mandate. [F] (AR2026 p.176) (AR2026 p.184) (AR2026 p.41) The reservations are the unresolved whistle-blower investigations, the audit-trail data-residency exception, the trebled contingent liability, and an exceptional-item presentation that flatters the metric management guides on. [F] (AR2026 p.188) (AR2026 p.179) (AR2026 p.324) [AI] None of these is a reason to distrust the numbers; each is a reason to ask a question. [AI]

**This is the finding we would put first in a governance discussion.** Net non-goods charges from the group to CIL more than doubled, from Rs 185.34 crore to Rs 451.74 crore, taking them from 1.78% to 3.72% of revenue - an increase equal to 8.6% of pre-tax profit in a year when reported margin rose by only one percentage point. [E] (AR2026 p.245) The only explanation offered was for the royalty component: 'we had some different royalty percentages for different services, which used to range between 1% to 8%. We have standardized it to 4%. That's all... nothing more.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) **No explanation at all has been offered for the doubling of support services or the 92% increase in reimbursements paid**, and the FY27 authorisation contemplates a further Rs 216.92 crore of services received and a new Rs 118.77 crore 'Transfer of Technology' charge to Cummins Inc. [F] (AR2026 p.398) An analyst noted on the Q1 FY27 call that royalty and support services had reached 2.5% of sales 'and indications are it's going to go further up in fiscal 27'; the answer addressed only royalty standardisation. [F] [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

**On the transfer-pricing mechanism itself.** The disclosed basis is specific and, for once, transparent: CIL sells manufactured engines and gensets to group entities at 'Cost plus at least 11% mark-up' and manufactured components and spares at 'Cost plus 14% mark-up' or prices charged to third-party dealers; it buys engines for manufacturing from CTIPL at 'Cost plus 11% markup', turbochargers and components at 'third party pricing', and components and spares for distribution at 'Cost plus 5% markup'; royalty is '4% of eligible sales'; and reimbursements are at actual cost. [F] (AR2026 p.401) Arm's length is tested 'internally by the management' using transfer-pricing methods, and 'A copy of the valuation or other external party report' is marked 'Not applicable'. [F] (AR2026 p.401) (AR2026 p.400) The statutory auditor confirms compliance with Sections 177 and 188, and there is a live transfer-pricing dispute of Rs 2.69 crore for AY2021-22 and Rs 1.30 crore for AY2022-23 before appellate authorities. [F] (AR2026 p.188) (AR2026 p.185) (AR2026 p.186) **The substantive point for a minority shareholder is that an 11% cost-plus on exports to a fellow subsidiary caps CIL's margin on that revenue at 11% over cost, however profitable the end market.** With FY27 sale-of-goods approval to Cummins Limited UK of Rs 1,974.78 crore against Rs 1,018.25 crore actual, the mix effect of that cap could become material. [F] (AR2026 p.398) [AI]

items: **No guarantees in either direction.** 'There have been no guarantees provided or received for any related party receivables or payables', outstanding balances are 'unsecured and interest free and settlement occurs in cash', and no impairment has ever been recorded on related-party receivables. **The institutional register is rotating, however.** Foreign institutional holding rose from 16.45% in September 2023 to 21.19% in June 2026, while domestic institutional holding fell from 21.97% to 19.06% - foreigners have bought roughly 4.7 percentage points from domestic institutions over eleven quarters. [F] (NUMBERS) [E] Public holding is stable at 8.65% and the shareholder count is 173,450. [F] (NUMBERS)

**CIL is a Foreign Owned and Controlled Company** under the FEMA non-debt instrument rules, which constrains its downstream investment activity - the Clean Max investment required a separate auditor compliance certificate, which was issued unqualified. [F] (AR2026 p.36)

**No promoter-group receivable or payable concentration risk.** Related-party receivables are Rs 480.44 crore, 17.4% of total receivables, against related-party payables of Rs 959.51 crore - CIL is a net payer to the group, so the counterparty credit exposure runs in CIL's favour. [E] (AR2026 p.251)

**Related-party governance process.** The Audit and Compliance Committee and Board approved FY26 transactions on five dates through the year and FY27 limits on 24 March and 27 May 2026; shareholder approvals were obtained at the AGM of 8 August 2025 and by postal ballot on 5 January 2026; and a session on related-party transactions was conducted for directors during the year. [F] (AR2026 p.49) (AR2026 p.394) (AR2026 p.133) The process is diligent. The substance - internally tested cost-plus formulas with no external valuation - is where the exposure sits. [AI]

items: **Promoter holding has not moved at all.** Cummins Inc. holds 141,372,000 shares, exactly 51.00%, in every one of the twelve quarters from September 2023 to June 2026; promoter change over one year is recorded as 0.0. [F] (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.91) No promoter share pledge is disclosed anywhere. [F] (AR2026, searched)

**No director or KMP shareholding in CIL is disclosed anywhere in the annual report.** [F] (AR2026, searched) The report states only that there is 'no pecuniary relationship or transactions of any of the Non-executive Directors vis-a-vis the Company, apart from the remuneration as detailed in this Report'. [F] (AR2026 p.77) Executive alignment therefore rests on parent-company equity, not on CIL equity. [AI]

**The company has no stock option scheme of its own.** 'The Company does not have a Stock Option Scheme and no severance fees are payable to any Director.' [F] (AR2026 p.77) The Managing Director's Rs 1.26 crore of 'other benefits' 'includes stock options of Holding Company and other perquisites', and Rs 14.38 crore was credited to equity in FY26 as a contribution from Cummins Inc. for share-based payments, cumulatively Rs 59.92 crore. [F] (AR2026 p.77) (AR2026 p.197) Management is therefore incentivised on Cummins Inc.'s share price, not CIL's - an alignment gap that is rarely discussed and is structurally important when transfer pricing between the two is set internally. [AI]

**Institutional ownership is rotating from domestic to foreign hands.** Foreign institutional holding rose from 16.45% in September 2023 to 21.19% in June 2026; domestic institutional holding fell from 21.97% to 19.06% over the same period; public holding is steady at 8.65% and the register has 173,450 shareholders. [F] (NUMBERS) [E] Within the March 2026 snapshot, mutual funds hold 12.57%, banks, financial institutions and insurers 3.98% and corporate bodies 0.49%. [F] (AR2026 p.91)

**Dividend alignment is strong and rising.** FY26 dividend of Rs 66 per share (Rs 20 interim plus Rs 46 final) against Rs 51.50, a payout of 77% of consolidated profit and Rs 1,483.02 crore in cash, of which Rs 756.34 crore went to Cummins Inc. [F] (AR2026 p.29) (AR2026 p.245) (NUMBERS) The parent takes its return as dividend rather than as anything more exotic, which is a positive; but with free cash flow of Rs 1,487 crore almost exactly equal to the dividend, the payout is now at its practical ceiling. Genuinely granular where it chooses to be: node-level power-generation revenue, industrial sub-segment revenue and data-centre shares are given voluntarily on calls, which is more than most Indian capital-goods companies provide. [AI] What it is not is a management team that is independent of, or incentivised alongside, the minority shareholders whose capital it deploys - and on the three issues where that distinction bites (transfer pricing, disclosure of the things that would let minorities test transfer pricing, and succession), the scores are 4, 5 and 3. sections.title: Competition: named but unquantified, with the only disclosed financials belonging to group companies

blocks.text: **No competitor financials are disclosed anywhere in the documents in this folder.** There is no peer-comparison table in the annual report, no market-share data ('we do not have any syndicated market research for that'), and no listed-comparable analysis. [F] (AR2026, searched) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) The only entities for which the company discloses revenue, profit and net worth are its own related parties, in the AGM related-party schedule. We present those below because they are informative about where value sits inside the group - not because they are competitors. [AI]

blocks.caption: Entities with financials disclosed in the documents (all are Cummins group related parties, not competitors)
rows: Cummins Generator Technologies India Private Limited (48.74% associate)

blocks.text: Sources: AGM related-party schedule for Cummins Inc., Cummins Limited UK, CTIPL and TCPL; Directors' Report and AOC-1 for VCPL and CGTIPL; consolidated statements for CIL. [F] (AR2026 p.396) (AR2026 p.30) (AR2026 p.45) (AR2026 p.276) Profit-after-tax figures for VCPL and CGTIPL are the sum of the amounts considered and not considered in consolidation; net worth grossing is our arithmetic from the attributable figures. [E] Return on net worth, price-to-earnings and dated market comparisons are not disclosed for any of these entities. [F]

**The most instructive line in that table is CTIPL.** A fellow subsidiary of the same parent, unlisted, operating in India, with FY25 revenue of Rs 9,476.46 crore - 91% of CIL's FY25 revenue - a 15.8% net margin and a return on net worth of about 36%. [E] (AR2026 p.396) CIL buys Rs 1,317.31 crore of goods from it and is seeking authorisation for up to Rs 4,092.99 crore of transactions with it in FY27. [F] (AR2026 p.248) (AR2026 p.394) A minority shareholder in CIL has no economic interest in CTIPL whatsoever. When management says it manufactures 'in CIL what we can' and elsewhere 'if there is scale in some other entity', the allocation decision between two similarly sized, similarly profitable Indian entities - one listed, one wholly owned by the parent - is made by people who sit on CIL's board. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) [AI] Nothing in the documents suggests misallocation; equally, nothing in the documents would reveal it. [AI]

blocks.text: **A telling detail about the labour market as a competitive dimension.** Asked whether local competitors hiring senior people from Cummins was hurting the business, management answered: 'Cummins has been a ground where almost all competition hires from Cummins. So, this is not new to us. The company has been around in India for 60-plus years, backed by a great brand, technology and innovation, and we continue to have excellent manpower with us already.' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) Permanent employee attrition was 7% and permanent worker attrition 4%, both down year on year, which is consistent with that answer. [F] (AR2026 p.125) [AI]
The market splits cleanly into three competitive regimes, and CIL's position is very different in each. [AI]

items: **Above 2,500 kVA (data centres, mega-infrastructure): oligopoly, and CIL is inside it.** A handful of multinationals with the products, project-execution capability and service commitments to satisfy 99.99%-uptime customers. Management says 'we do get invited by all customers when they have inquiries' and that the intensity 'has remained the same'. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) (CALL Jun 2026) The competitive basis is lead time, solution capability and lifetime service, not unit price. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) **This is the profit pool the market is paying for, and CIL's position looks genuinely strong - but is entirely unquantified.** [AI]

**Below 800 kW (CPCB IV+ mainstream): fragmented and hardening.** Ten to twelve competitors, all with compliant product ranges, established channels and brands, and pricing described as 'Very, very aggressive... extremely aggressive, especially in the power generation space'. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) The annual report concedes 'pricing pressure is intensifying across the industry'. **Aftermarket: local, dense and defensible, but being nibbled.** 450 touchpoints, 3,500 trained engineers, two-hour critical response and a 90% NPS are real barriers, and management says third-party intensity has not increased. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) (CALL Nov 2025) [F] (AR2026 p.18) Against that, the company's own threats section flags will-fit parts and OEM second-line brands, and management has acknowledged that as the unorganised channel learns CPCB IV+ technology 'some of this market share could start going away'. [F] (AR2026 p.54) [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)

**Exports: no franchise.** Management says plainly that CIL does not understand these markets as well as India, faces Chinese competition in Africa and the Middle East, credit constraints in Latin America and structural weakness in Europe, and will not guide growth. [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) (CALL Feb 2026)

blocks.text: **The assessment that follows.** CIL's competitive position is strongest exactly where disclosure is weakest, and weakest exactly where disclosure is strongest. [AI] An investor can verify, quarter by quarter, that the low and medium horsepower business is growing in the low single digits in a price war; the investor cannot verify anything at all about the high-horsepower position that justifies the multiple. [F] (CALL Aug 2026) [E] [AI] Management's refusal to discuss market share is defensible on the stated grounds that no syndicated data exists, but it also means the central competitive claim in the bull case is untestable from the outside. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) [AI]

sections.title: Moat scorecard: an installed-base and approvals moat, not a technology moat

blocks.caption: Moat-factor scorecard (1 = none, 10 = very strong)
rows: Over six decades in India; 'backed by a great brand, technology and innovation'; a 90% Net Promoter Score, the highest achieved anywhere in the Cummins group; and the fact that 'almost all competition hires from Cummins'. Management's stated value proposition - 'a backup genset is used as an insurance that it will work on the day when you need it to work even if it is for 10 minutes in a whole year' - is precisely the kind of low-frequency, high-consequence purchase where brand dominates [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) (CALL Nov 2025) [F] (AR2026 p.18)

Real but asymmetric. Once an asset is installed, the servicing relationship is sticky: two-year comprehensive warranty, optional five-year extended warranty, comprehensive maintenance contracts, telematics, predictive maintenance and a two-hour response commitment. Data-centre customers receive 'a very separate focus' in the aftermarket. But the genset itself is a competitively bid capital purchase each time, and will-fit parts erode the aftermarket lock [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) (CALL Jun 2026) (CALL Aug 2026) [F] (AR2026 p.54)

The strongest structural factor. The entire sub-800 kW range was redesigned for CPCB IV+; retrofit emission control device approvals were obtained for CPCB I and II engines; Euro Stage V, Tier III, Stage IIIA and Euro III certifications were achieved for exports; CEV BS V and Trem IV/V were rolled out; FM/UL certification was obtained for pump engines; 25 Quality Control Orders were onboarded for BIS compliance; and Indian Railways granted serial-production approval for Hotel Load Converters. Each is a fixed cost a smaller competitor must fund repeatedly [F] (AR2026 p.33) (AR2026 p.21) (AR2026 p.15)

The technology is the parent's, not CIL's. Own R&D was Rs 10.54 crore, 0.09% of sales, of which only Rs 4.65 crore was revenue expenditure. Intangibles consist of Rs 85.67 crore of technical know-how (amortising, no additions in FY26) and Rs 13.78 crore of development cost. Royalty of 4% of eligible sales is paid for the technology, and a further Rs 118.77 crore 'Transfer of Technology' charge is proposed for FY27. CIL is a licensee with excellent application engineering, not an IP owner [F] (AR2026 p.34) (AR2026 p.212) (AR2026 p.401) (AR2026 p.398) [AI]

The widest domestic range (2.8 to 100 litres, gensets to 3,750 kVA); localised QSK60 giving a cost advantage over importing competitors at the node that matters today; fixed-asset turnover of 5.10x; 26,000+ gensets delivered in a year; and India-made cylinder blocks validated for global use. The limits: the advantage is node-specific and expires if the market moves to 78L and 95L, and 52% of purchases are bought from group entities at cost-plus, which caps how much of the scale benefit CIL retains [F] (SCREENER) (AR2026 p.17) (AR2026 p.23) (AR2026 p.136) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) [AI]

480+ 4S touchpoints, 110+ retail touchpoints, 133 GOEM dealers, 179 dealers and distributors, 3,500 trained engineers across 450 touchpoints, 877,569 service orders, multi-year Track Maintenance Machine orders, three-year AMCs, new and renewed rate contracts across mining, infrastructure and railways, and supplier-partnership awards from four named construction OEMs. Working with data-centre customers 'even before they start floating their requests' is the clearest evidence of relationship depth [F] (AR2026 p.10) (AR2026 p.56) (AR2026 p.136) (AR2026 p.18) (AR2026 p.15) (AR2026 p.55) (AR2026 p.14) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

There are none. An installed base is not a network: no customer gains value because another customer bought a Cummins genset. The density of the service network creates scale economics in coverage, which is a cost advantage, not a network effect. We score this low deliberately because it is frequently mislabelled in this sector [AI]

Weak, and structurally so. 52% of purchases come from related parties; alternators come from a 48.74%-owned associate exposed to copper; the QSK95 is imported; battery energy storage has no local supply chain; and management cites supplier labour shortages, freight and global node contention as live constraints. Mitigations disclosed are dual sourcing, adjusted payment terms with financially weaker suppliers and long-term supplier agreements [F] (AR2026 p.136) (AR2026 p.30) (AR2026 p.59) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) (CALL Aug 2026)
Eight factors, unweighted. Not a rating [E]

subsections.title: The two questions these scores cannot answer

items: **1. Is market share rising, flat or falling?** Every moat score above is about capability, not outcome. The outcome measure - share - is unavailable: 'we do not have any syndicated market research for that', 'If there was a syndicated research, which would tell me that this is exactly the volume of power gen sold in the market, if there was any registration for gensets, I could have said that to you. But in the lack of that data, it will be very difficult to say', and, when asked directly whether share beyond data centres was intact, 'I cannot share anything on market share, unfortunately.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) (CALL Nov 2025) A moat that cannot be measured in share terms is a hypothesis. [AI]

**2. Does the moat survive the node migration and the aftermarket learning curve?** Two specific transitions are visible and neither is resolved. If Indian data centres move from QSK60 to QSK78 and QSK95, CIL imports like everybody else and its cost differentiation becomes service differentiation - management's clear line of sight is only two years. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) And if the unorganised channel learns to service CPCB IV+ machines, management has already conceded 'some of this market share could start going away'. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) The scores above assume neither happens within the forecast horizon; the company has not said that they will not. [AI]

blocks.text: This is a **distribution-and-approvals moat wrapped around a licensed technology**, and it is stronger than the average Indian capital-goods franchise but narrower than the multiple implies. [AI] The two factors that score 8 - brand and regulatory barriers - are the ones that have actually driven the FY24-FY26 result, and both are durable: a CPCB-style norm change recurs every several years and each one costs a competitor a full product redesign, while a 90% NPS on an insurance-like purchase is not bought with price. [F] (AR2026 p.33) (AR2026 p.18) [AI] The two factors that score 4 and below - technology ownership and input control - are the ones that determine how much of the economics CIL keeps rather than remits to the group, and both moved against minorities in FY26 as royalty, support services and reimbursements rose from 1.78% to 3.72% of revenue. [E] (AR2026 p.245) [AI]

The honest summary is that CIL has a strong competitive position and a weak ownership position over the sources of that position. [AI] The board notes in this dashboard describe an installed-base and emissions-compliance moat and are explicit that it is 'a reasoned view from public industry structure, not a claim verified against an external source'. [BOARD] Our work in these documents supports the reasoning and adds the qualification that the moat is real, the share evidence is absent, and the economics of the moat are shared with a parent that sets the prices. [AI]

subsections.title: Why TAM cannot be translated into company revenue

blocks.text: **Illustrative share arithmetic, labelled as arithmetic and nothing more [E].** CIL's FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 12,143.19 crore is about 1.0% of the Rs 12.2 lakh crore Union Budget FY27 capital expenditure figure. [E] (AR2026 p.29) (AR2026 p.51) If one imagined CIL capturing 2% of that single-year number, revenue would roughly double; if 0.5%, it would halve. That arithmetic is worthless, and it is worth stating why, because this is exactly the calculation that supports most bullish notes on Indian capital goods. [AI]

items: **A genset is a fraction of a percent of a project's capex.** Nothing in the documents links infrastructure spend to genset demand with any conversion ratio, and the company has never published one. [F]

**The company itself refuses the conversion.** On the budget capex announcement: 'We are watching the segments in which they have announced the capex flow. We are waiting to see how that gets converted into projects that could lead for demand for our products. It takes a little bit of time.' [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) On the data-centre tax break: 'we are waiting to see how this translates into real orders.' [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) On data-centre announcements generally: 'announcement to execution could be anywhere between a 1 to 2-year timeline.' [MC] (CALL Nov 2025)

**The genset-per-megawatt ratio is explicitly not derivable.** Asked how many gensets a megawatt of data-centre load requires, management answered: 'that can be very different depending on how the data centers design their entire location. That can vary.' [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) So even the data-centre TAM cannot be converted into units.

**Backup power is a small, discretionary slice of the power market and the deficit is closing.** The company's own presentation shows India's energy deficit falling to 0.1% and peak deficit to 0.4-0.5% by FY25 - the trend that historically drove genset demand has largely run its course, which is why the growth now comes from mission-critical uptime (data centres, hospitals) rather than from grid unreliability. [F] (PPT Feb 2025) [AI]

**TAM growth and CIL growth have visibly diverged already.** India's infrastructure narrative has been intact throughout FY25 and FY26, yet CIL's domestic Industrial revenue fell 1% in FY26, construction was flat in Q1 FY27, road construction is running at 'half the rate of what it was in the previous year', and mining tenders 'still haven't seen those tenders come up'. [F] (CALL Jun 2026) (CALL Aug 2026) [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) TAM was not the binding constraint. [AI]

blocks.text: The useful conclusion from the bottom-up framing is that CIL's revenue is not TAM-constrained; it is constrained by three things the TAM does not describe: how many machines Indian buyers install each year, how large those machines are, and what share of the resulting installed base CIL manages to service. [AI] Only the first is macro-driven. [AI]

items: **Concentration differs sharply by node.** Above 2,500 kVA: 'a few players' with 'the number of players is slightly smaller in the higher horsepower range', competing on solution and lead time. [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) (CALL Feb 2026) Below 800 kW: 'more than 10 or 12 competitors', 'very, very high' intensity, 'extremely aggressive' pricing. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) (CALL Feb 2026) The industry is therefore an oligopoly at the top and commoditising at the bottom, and CIL's mix is migrating upward. [AI]

**Channel structure.** Three channels operate in parallel: direct sales to large end customers and hyperscalers; a Genset OEM dealer network that grew to 133 dealers plus 14 newly appointed '2S' dealers for the low-kVA segment; and industrial OEMs who embed CIL engines in their equipment. [F] (AR2026 p.56) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) Total dealers and distributors number 179, up from 165, with the top ten accounting for 72% of dealer sales in both years, and dealers accounting for 16% of total sales. [F] (AR2026 p.136)

**The service channel is the deeper structure.** 480+ 4S (sales, spares, service, surveys) touchpoints, 110+ retail touchpoints, one parts distribution centre, and with dealers 3,500 trained engineers across 450 touchpoints. [F] (AR2026 p.10) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) In FY26 the company appointed its first channel partner from outside the Cummins fraternity in nearly four decades - Island Prime Power in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands - which signals a willingness to widen the channel where the legacy network does not reach. [F] (AR2026 p.20) [AI]

**Supplier structure.** Highly concentrated toward the group: 52% of purchases from related parties, only 1% from trading houses across 23 trading houses, with the top ten trading houses at 95% of that 1%. [F] (AR2026 p.136) (AR2026 p.135) Suppliers covering 76% of total spend were included in ESG and BRSR awareness programmes. [F] (AR2026 p.136)

**Regulatory structure is the key industry variable.** CPCB IV+ has reset the domestic genset market; the company believes no further norm is on the horizon either below or above 800 kW 'for the next few years'; CAQM and NGT retrofit mandates create a separate aftermarket; ORCM Stage V is pending for construction equipment with timing 'particularly for tracked excavator applications' uncertain; and CEMM V marine norms arrive in 2028. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) [F] (AR2026 p.52) (AR2026 p.53) (PPT Feb 2025) Each transition redistributes share toward whoever is certified first. [AI]

[F] (AR2026 p.50) CIL's own exports grew 12% to a level within the range of the prior several years, were flat in Q1 FY27, and management says 'these are not the end markets that we understand as well as the India market'. [F] (CALL Aug 2026) [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) The macro claim is not evidenced in the company's numbers. [AI]

blocks.text: Two themes are structurally sound and are already in the numbers: **regulatory capability** and the **aftermarket annuity**. Together they explain most of the durable part of the FY24-FY26 re-rating and they should persist through a cycle. [AI] One theme - **data centres** - is a genuine and large demand pool where CIL is clearly winning, but where the evidence is a revenue share disclosed on a call rather than a contract, a backlog or a market share, and where the company's own annual report warns about execution-timing variability. [F] (AR2026 p.51) [AI] Three themes - **defence and marine indigenisation, export manufacturing base, and energy storage** - are capability stories with negligible or zero revenue, correctly valued as options rather than earnings. [AI] And several themes that circulate around this stock - AI TAM conversion, hydrogen, China-plus-one, residential premiumisation - are either third-party macro or have been explicitly contradicted by management. The structural test that matters: **would this company still compound at high-teens rates if data-centre revenue stopped growing tomorrow?** On the FY26 and Q1 FY27 evidence, the answer is no - the rest of domestic power generation grew in the low single digits in Q1 FY27, domestic industrial fell 1% in FY26, exports were flat in Q1 FY27, and only distribution at +14% would still be compounding. [E] (CALL Aug 2026) (CALL Jun 2026) That is the single most important structural conclusion in this report, and it is a conclusion about concentration, not about quality. [AI]

sections.title: Earnings quality: audited and real, but persistently cash-light

blocks.caption: PAT versus operating cash flow, ten years (Rs crore, consolidated, from our statements data)

blocks.text: All figures from our statements data; sums and ratios are our arithmetic. [F] (NUMBERS) [E] The company's own cash flow statement confirms FY26 operating cash flow of Rs 1,734.26 crore against Rs 1,682.59 crore. [F] (AR2026 p.278) Free cash flow was Rs 1,487 crore in FY26, Rs 3,955 crore cumulatively over three years and Rs 5,402 crore over five. [F] (NUMBERS)

**The diagnosis matters more than the ratio.** A CFO/PAT ratio below 1.0x in nine of ten years is a pattern, not a blip, and it deserves an explanation. Three candidate explanations, tested: [AI] (1) **Aggressive revenue recognition** - not supported. The single key audit matter is revenue recognition and the auditor tested cut-off, journal entries and variable consideration and issued an unmodified opinion; receivable ageing improved; the expected credit loss rate fell to 0.30%; and credit-impaired receivables fell. [F] (AR2026 p.176) (AR2026 p.177) (AR2026 p.221) (2) **Non-cash profit** - partly true. Rs 266.28 crore of FY26 profit is equity-accounted from a joint venture and an associate, but Rs 216.75 crore of that was actually received as cash dividends, shown in investing rather than operating cash flow - so the 'non-cash' element is largely a classification effect. [F] (AR2026 p.276) (AR2026 p.278) [AI] (3) **Growth-driven working capital** - the main explanation. Working capital absorbed Rs 503.09 crore in FY26 and Rs 72.11 crore in FY25, against revenue growth of 17% and 15%. [F] (AR2026 p.278) A company growing at these rates with 83 debtor days and 56 inventory days will structurally consume cash. [AI]

The practical consequence of a 0.76x five-year ratio is that **reported earnings overstate distributable cash by roughly a quarter through the cycle.** [E] At the current 77% payout ratio, FY26 free cash flow of Rs 1,487 crore covered the Rs 1,483.02 crore dividend by four crore. [F] (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.279) [E] There is no longer a cushion: another year of similar working-capital absorption on slower profit growth would have to be funded from the Rs 3,925 crore treasury. [AI] That is affordable for many years; it is not a rising-dividend story without rising cash conversion. [AI]

**The tax rate is stable and unremarkable.** 23% in FY26, and 22-23% in eight of the last ten years, with the exceptions of FY19 (31%) and FY20 (13%, the year of the corporate tax rate change). [F] (NUMBERS) FY26 included Rs 12.56 crore of tax for earlier years. [F] (AR2026 p.192) There is no evidence of tax-driven earnings management. [AI]

[F] (AR2026 p.184) (AR2026 p.188) (AR2026 p.274) [AI]

The three qualifications an investor should carry forward are: [AI] (1) through the cycle, roughly 24% of reported profit does not convert to operating cash, so a price-to-earnings multiple of 59.7x corresponds to a materially higher multiple of operating cash flow; [E] (NUMBERS) (2) 25.4% of pre-tax profit comes from interest, rent, investment gains and an equity-accounted stake in two companies CIL does not control - assets that should be valued separately from the engine business rather than capitalised at the engine business's multiple; [E] (AR2026 p.276) (AR2026 p.318) [AI] and (3) the metric management guides on, 'profit before tax before exceptional items', excludes a Rs 94.20 crore labour-code charge that represents a permanent increase in employee obligations and whose ongoing cost will flow through operating lines from FY27. [F] (AR2026 p.262) (AR2026 p.243) [AI] On a scale where a typical Indian listed industrial sits around 6, we would score earnings quality **5 out of 10** - clean accounting, mediocre cash conversion, and a meaningful non-operating component. sections.title: Forecast: the base-case model, its drivers, and what it deliberately ignores

blocks.text: Our DCF model builds a five-year free cash flow to the firm as **EBITDA less tax on EBIT less capex less the change in net working capital**, with revenue growth fading linearly from a starting rate to a year-five rate, a Gordon terminal value beyond year five, and equity value derived as enterprise value less borrowings. [F] (NUMBERS) Every projected figure in this section comes from that model; we interpret it and do not extend it. [AI]

blocks.text: Two input choices deserve flagging before the output is read, because they drive most of the result. [AI] First, **the 20% EBITDA margin is above the latest quarter's 18%** and equal to the trailing-twelve-month figure, so the base case already assumes the Q1 FY27 compression reverses. [F] (NUMBERS) Second, **the equity bridge deducts borrowings without adding cash**, and the audited balance sheet carries Rs 500.01 crore of cash, Rs 1,874.06 crore of other bank balances and Rs 1,548.43 crore of current investments, plus Rs 602.09 crore of equity-method investments and investment property with a Rs 1,485.52 crore fair value. [F] (AR2026 p.274) (AR2026 p.216) None of that is in the per-share output. [AI]

blocks.text: All figures from our DCF model. [F] (NUMBERS) Fiscal-year labels are ours and approximate, because the base is a trailing-twelve-month period ending in June rather than a March year end. [AI]

**Driver commentary [AI].** The projection embeds a business that roughly doubles revenue over five years while holding margin flat, converts a rising share of EBITDA into free cash flow (FCFF rises from 43.7% of EBITDA in year 1 to 52.2% in year 5 as growth - and therefore working-capital absorption and growth capex - fades), and is then capitalised in perpetuity at 5.5% growth. [E] (NUMBERS) Seventy-two per cent of the enterprise value sits in the terminal value, which is normal for a growing company at a 15% discount rate but means the output is far more sensitive to the terminal assumptions than to anything in the explicit five years. [E] (NUMBERS)

items: **Revenue = units x realisation per unit, across four books.** Domestic power generation (Rs 4,758 crore FY26, growing on data-centre projects and a low-single-digit non-data-centre core), distribution (Rs 3,278 crore, growing on installed base and attach rate), domestic industrial (Rs 1,650 crore, growing on Indian Railways, mining, marine and construction tender cadence) and exports (Rs 1,989 crore, channel and geography driven). [F] (CALL Jun 2026) (AR2026 p.13)

**Node mix is the second-order revenue driver.** Q1 FY27 power generation split roughly Rs 77 crore low horsepower, Rs 248 crore medium, Rs 125 crore heavy duty and about Rs 974 crore high horsepower - so a mix shift up the range lifts revenue per unit materially even at flat unit volumes. [F] (CALL Aug 2026) [E]

**EBITDA margin = gross margin (36.8% in FY26) less employee cost (6.5%) less other expenses (8.9%).** The volatile term is gross margin, geared roughly 3.0x EBITDA to every 1% move in net material cost. [E] (AR2026 p.276)

**Price recovery lag is the timing driver.** Cost hits immediately; price realisation follows 'at least a quarter' because of power-generation backlogs, and recovery is incomplete. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

**Working capital is the cash driver.** The model assumes 49 days; the company ran 53 in FY26 and a 60-day cash conversion cycle, so the model is slightly more optimistic than the latest actual. [F] (NUMBERS) [E]

**Capex is barely a driver at all.** At 2.0% of sales with 70-75% utilisation and 'no major capital expenditure plan', reinvestment is not the constraint on growth - which is exactly why FCFF conversion improves as growth fades. [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) [E]

**Non-operating income is outside the model entirely.** Rs 517.34 crore of other income and Rs 266.28 crore of equity-accounted profit are excluded from an EBITDA-based FCFF, as are the assets that generate them. [F] (AR2026 p.276) (AR2026 p.318) [AI]

subsections.title: What the forecast deliberately does not assume

items: **No order-book visibility.** Nothing is disclosed, so nothing is modelled. [F] (AR2026, searched)

**No margin expansion above 20%**, despite management stating 'definitely, there is scope to improve our margins here on'. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) The base case is flat margin; the bull case tests 22%. [F] (NUMBERS)

**No revenue from battery energy storage, defence platforms, hydrogen or 78-litre localisation.** All four are capability announcements with zero or immaterial disclosed revenue. [F] (AR2026 p.16) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)
**No acquisition, no capital raise and no change in share count.** The company raised nothing in FY26, has no stock option scheme and has 277,200,000 shares. [F] (AR2026 p.30) (AR2026 p.77)

**No change in the relationship with the 51% parent** - the royalty rate, the cost-plus formulas and the related-party caps are held as they are. A tightening or loosening of any of these would move earnings without any operating change. [F] (AR2026 p.401) [AI]

**No monetisation or re-rating of the treasury or the property.** Rs 3,925 crore of cash, deposits and liquid investments, Rs 602.09 crore of equity-method stakes and investment property with a Rs 1,485.52 crore fair value contribute nothing to the per-share output. [F] (AR2026 p.274) (AR2026 p.216) [AI]

**No explicit data-centre assumption.** The model forecasts the company, not the segment. Given that data centres are now 40% of power-generation revenue, that is a material abstraction. [F] (CALL Aug 2026) [AI]

**No cyclical downturn inside the explicit five years.** Growth fades from 16% to 10% but never turns negative, even though revenue fell in FY20 and FY21 and one quarter in FY26 saw power generation decline 16% year on year. [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) [AI]

sections.title: Scenarios: three futures, none of which reaches the share price

blocks.caption: Scenario table, entirely from our DCF model
rows: Growth decelerates to roughly GDP-plus and margin reverts to the FY22-FY23 level
Trend growth is maintained and fades gradually; margin holds at the trailing level
Data-centre-led acceleration with margin expansion beyond the FY26 peak

blocks.caption: Scenario cash-flow paths, from our DCF model (Rs crore)

blocks.text: A detail worth noticing: **year-one free cash flow is almost identical across all three scenarios** - Rs 1,154.3 crore in the bear case, Rs 1,284.9 crore in the base and Rs 1,276.8 crore in the bull. [F] (NUMBERS) In the bull case, faster growth consumes more working capital and more capex, offsetting the higher margin in year one; the bull case only pulls away from years two to five. [E] The corollary is that the next twelve months of cash flow tell an investor almost nothing about which scenario is unfolding; only the growth and margin trajectory does. [AI]
We will not assign decimal probabilities to scenarios built on a single starting-growth parameter. [AI] What can be said, evidence by evidence: [AI]

items: **The base case's 16% starting growth is close to what the company is actually doing.** Q1 FY27 net sales grew 18% and domestic 22%; three-year sales growth is 16.0% and five-year 22.7%. [F] (CALL Aug 2026) (NUMBERS) The growth assumption is unaggressive. [AI]

**The base case's 20% margin is more demanding than it looks.** It is above the Q1 FY27 actual of 18% and requires the commodity and employee-cost step-up to be recovered. Management has taken one price increase, says recovery will be incomplete, and will not forecast the landing point. [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) [AI]

**The bear case's 16% margin is not a stress test - it is the FY22 and FY23 reality.** Operating margin was 14% in FY22 and 16% in FY23. [F] (NUMBERS) A bear case that returns margin to a level achieved three years ago, alongside 5-6% growth, is entirely reachable if the domestic genset price war deepens while data-centre execution pauses. [AI]

**The bull case requires two things simultaneously that have never co-existed.** A 24.6% starting growth rate has been achieved (FY22 and FY23 both exceeded it), and a 22% margin has never been achieved in the ten years of data - the peak is 21% in FY26, which management itself said was flattered by non-repeatable items. [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) The bull case therefore asks for a first-ever margin at a growth rate last seen in a post-pandemic recovery year. [AI]

**Our qualitative weighting:** the base case is the central expectation; the bear case is more reachable than its label suggests and should carry meaningful weight given the Q1 margin print and the acknowledged pricing intensity below high horsepower; the bull case requires an unprecedented margin and should carry the least weight. [AI] Crucially, **the weighting barely matters for the conclusion**, because the spread from bear to bull is Rs 448.9 to Rs 1,039.7 against a share price of Rs 5,100. [F] (NUMBERS)

blocks.caption: Sensitivity of base-case value per share to WACC and terminal growth, from our DCF model (Rs per share)

blocks.text: **Reading the grid [AI].** The full nine-cell range is Rs 616.2 to Rs 996.0 - a 62% spread across a three-point WACC range and a two-point terminal-growth range. That is a wide band in relative terms and an irrelevant one in absolute terms: **the most generous cell is still 80% below the share price.** [E] (NUMBERS) The grid's practical message is that no plausible discount-rate or terminal-growth debate reconciles this model to this price. Closing the gap would require changes of a different order: a materially lower cost of equity than 15%, a materially higher terminal growth than 6.5%, a margin well above any level the company has achieved, the addition of the Rs 3,925 crore treasury and Rs 1,485.52 crore of property fair value to the equity bridge, and the capitalisation of the Rs 266.28 crore equity-accounted profit stream that the EBITDA-based model excludes. [F] (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.274) (AR2026 p.216) (AR2026 p.276) [AI] Each of those adjustments is individually defensible; collectively they still do not produce Rs 5,100, and we do not attempt the calculation because it would be a new valuation figure. [AI]

The value of this grid is diagnostic rather than prescriptive: it tells us the **model is not marginally wrong, it is categorically unable to reconcile the price**. That is itself the finding, and it reframes the question from 'what is this worth?' to 'what does the market believe that no discounted-cash-flow framework at a 15% cost of equity can express?' We take that question up in the priced-in section. [AI]

subsections.title: Multiples versus the disclosed peer set

blocks.text: **A peer-multiple comparison cannot be made from these documents.** No competitor revenue, margin, return on net worth or price-to-earnings figure is disclosed anywhere in the annual report, the transcripts, the presentation or the announcements. [F] (AR2026, searched) The only entities with disclosed financials are Cummins group related parties, and none of them has a disclosed market value. [F] (AR2026 p.396) Any peer multiple an investor sees in this name comes from outside these documents, and we will not import one. [AI]

What can be said with the disclosed group financials as context: CIL's FY26 net margin of 19.4% is the highest in the group set - against 15.8% at Cummins Technologies India (FY25), 13.5% at the alternator associate, 10.6% at Cummins Limited UK (CY2024), 8.4% at the parent (CY2025), 7.5% at the Valvoline joint venture and 7.3% at Tata Cummins (FY26). [E] (AR2026 p.396) (AR2026 p.30) (AR2026 p.45) (AR2026 p.276) That is a real and favourable fact about where profitability sits inside the Cummins system - CIL's genset and distribution mix earns more than components, lubricants or commercial-vehicle engines. [AI] It also means CIL is the group's highest-margin India entity while buying 52% of its purchases from group entities on cost-plus formulas: the arrangement as it currently stands favours CIL's reported margin. [F] (AR2026 p.136) (AR2026 p.401) [AI]

subsections.title: Interpreting the DCF and its assumptions

blocks.text: **Where the model is fair to the company.** The 16% starting growth is the median of three-year, five-year and trailing growth, not a low-balled figure. [F] (NUMBERS) The 20% margin is the trailing twelve-month level, not a trough. The capex rule is generous in the sense that it charges only depreciation plus growth capital at a 4.4x asset turnover - broadly what the company actually spends. [F] (NUMBERS) The 49-day working capital assumption is tighter than the FY26 actual of 53 days, which slightly helps the model's cash flows. [E] (NUMBERS) And the 5.5% terminal growth is a reasonable long-run nominal rate for an Indian industrial. [AI]

**Where the model is harsh.** Four places. [AI] (1) A 15% cost of equity - risk-free 7%, equity risk premium 7%, beta 1.15 - is the single largest driver of the result, and for a company with nil debt, 258x interest cover, a 40% ROCE, a 51% multinational parent and a 90% customer satisfaction score, a 15% required return is a demanding hurdle. [F] (NUMBERS) The sensitivity grid shows that moving to 13.5% adds about Rs 154 per share at 5.5% terminal growth. [E] (NUMBERS) (2) The equity bridge deducts Rs 37 crore of borrowings and adds no cash, ignoring Rs 3,925 crore of liquid assets. [F] (AR2026 p.274) (3) An EBITDA-based free cash flow excludes Rs 517.34 crore of interest, rent and investment income and Rs 266.28 crore of equity-accounted profit, and also excludes the assets behind them - investment property with a Rs 1,485.52 crore fair value and Rs 602.09 crore of joint-venture and associate carrying value. [F] (AR2026 p.318) (AR2026 p.276) (AR2026 p.216) (AR2026 p.274) (4) The model gives no credit for the operating-leverage option at 70-75% utilisation, because it forces growth capex at a fixed asset turnover. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) [AI]

**The honest net.** Correcting the four harsh features would raise the model's output meaningfully, in our judgement into the four-figure range rather than the high hundreds. [AI] It would not come close to Rs 5,100. **The conclusion an investor should take from the DCF is not a target - it is that the price is being set by something the DCF does not contain**, most plausibly a market view about the duration of high growth (a ten- or fifteen-year explicit period rather than five) combined with a much lower required return for a perceived quasi-monopoly on Indian data-centre backup power. [AI] Whether that view is correct is a judgement about the durability of a three-year-old revenue concentration, not about discount-rate arithmetic. [AI]

sections.title: What is priced in: the reverse DCF and how to read it honestly

blocks.caption: Reverse DCF, from our model
rows: Constant five-year sales CAGR implied by today's enterprise value
'Constant sales growth for five years, at the base margin and the same WACC and terminal growth, that makes the DCF equal today's EV'
The price requires roughly six times the base-case growth rate
Red: 'Price needs growth well above trend. Today's price implies about 78% a year sales growth for five years, against 13% in the base case'

blocks.text: All from our model and its rule-based red-flag output. [F] (NUMBERS) [E] For context on how far outside experience that number is: the company's own nine-year sales CAGR is 10.1%, its five-year is 22.7%, its three-year is 16.0%, and its best single year in the last decade was FY22 at 41.5% growth off a pandemic-depressed base. [F] (NUMBERS) [E] A 78% CAGR sustained for five years would take revenue from Rs 12,662 crore to roughly Rs 2.4 lakh crore. [E] (NUMBERS) No Indian capital-goods company has done that, and CIL's entire addressable structure - 26,000 gensets a year, 70-75% utilisation, no major capex plan - is inconsistent with it. [F] (AR2026 p.17) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) [AI]

**The forensic conclusion is not that the market expects 78% growth. It is that a five-year, 15%-WACC, EBITDA-only DCF cannot express this price at all, and that the price therefore embeds a set of beliefs that live outside the model.** [AI] Specifically, to justify Rs 5,100 an investor must hold at least three of the following simultaneously: [AI]

items: **A much longer explicit growth period.** Fifteen to twenty years of mid-teens compounding rather than five, which is the standard way high-quality Indian industrials are actually valued in practice. The evidence for durability is the aftermarket annuity and the regulatory barrier; the evidence against is that domestic industrial revenue fell 1% in FY26, exports are flat, and non-data-centre power generation grew in the low single digits in Q1 FY27. [F] (CALL Jun 2026) (CALL Aug 2026) [E] [AI]

**A much lower required return.** A debt-free, 40%-ROCE, 29.5%-ROE business with a multinational parent arguably deserves less than a 15% cost of equity - but the sensitivity grid shows that even 13.5% with 6.5% terminal growth gives Rs 996. [F] (NUMBERS) Discount-rate revision alone cannot do the work. [AI]

**A structurally higher terminal margin.** The bull case's 22% has never been achieved; FY26's 21% was flattered by one-time supplier benefits and mix that management called 'not repeatable'; Q1 FY27 was 18%. [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)

**Value for the assets the model excludes.** Rs 3,925 crore of cash and liquid investments, Rs 1,485.52 crore of investment-property fair value, and a Rs 266.28 crore equity-accounted profit stream from two businesses growing at 28% and 16%. [F] (AR2026 p.274) (AR2026 p.216) (AR2026 p.276) (AR2026 p.30) These are real and material, and worth roughly Rs 200 per share of gross asset value on the disclosed figures before any multiple is applied - which still leaves the bulk of the gap unexplained. [E] [AI]

**A re-rating premise rather than a cash-flow premise** - that scarcity of listed exposure to Indian data-centre power infrastructure, with a 51% multinational parent and a clean balance sheet, supports a multiple irrespective of five-year cash flow. That is a market-structure argument, not a valuation argument, and it is the one the reverse DCF is least able to test. [AI]

blocks.text: **The plain statement, which we will not soften:** on our model's assumptions the share price is roughly 6.7x the base-case fair value and 4.9x the bull-case fair value, and the model's rule-based screen flags this as a red item. [F] (NUMBERS) [E] Even after granting every criticism of the model set out above, the residual gap is not a rounding error - it is the dominant fact in this investment case, and it means an owner of the shares is underwriting duration and multiple persistence, not cash flow. [AI]
The strongest case against our own conclusion is that **the 78.1% figure is a model artefact and the model is the wrong tool for this asset**, and that case has real substance. [AI]

items: A five-year explicit period with a Gordon terminal value at 5.5% is a poor structure for a business whose competitive advantage is a multi-decade installed base that compounds mechanically. Every genset sold today generates aftermarket revenue for fifteen to twenty years; a five-year window captures the sale and almost none of the annuity. [F] (AR2026 p.18) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) [AI]

A 15% cost of equity with a 1.15 beta treats CIL as an average-risk cyclical. Its actual financial risk is close to zero: no debt, 258x interest cover, Rs 3,925 crore of liquid assets, no cash losses in a decade, and a 51% parent. [F] (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.189) (AR2026 p.274)

The model's own base case is internally conservative: it assumes no margin improvement despite management stating there is scope, no revenue from three announced new business lines, no utilisation-driven operating leverage, and no value for a third of the balance sheet. [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Reverse-DCF outputs above roughly 40% annual growth are mathematically unstable and stop carrying information: at that point the terminal value dominates so completely that the implied growth rate becomes a statement about the model rather than about market expectations. [AI]

Empirically, high-quality Indian industrial franchises with 40% ROCE and no debt have traded at 50-70x earnings for extended periods, and a discounted-cash-flow model with a 15% discount rate has been unable to justify any of them for years. Using this model as a market-timing signal would have been costly. [AI]

blocks.text: **Our resolution.** Both things are true. The reverse-DCF number is not a forecast of market expectations and should not be quoted as one. But the direction it points in is confirmed by every independent multiple: 59.7x trailing earnings on flat trailing earnings, 54.6x EV/EBITDA, 11.17x EV/sales and 16.67x book, in a business where a quarter of pre-tax profit is interest, rent and equity-accounted income, cash conversion is 0.76x through the cycle, growth is concentrated in three unnamed customers, and the latest quarter delivered 0.8% profit growth on 17.9% revenue growth. [F] (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.340) [E] **The defensible conclusion is that the valuation leaves no room for the cyclical, concentration and margin risks this report has documented - not that a precise fair value of Rs 757.6 is the answer.** [AI]

sections.title: Final thesis

blocks.text: Cummins India is one of a small number of Indian industrial businesses that has genuinely earned its returns. [AI] Revenue has grown from Rs 4,360 crore in FY21 to Rs 12,143 crore in FY26 on cumulative capex of roughly Rs 832 crore, taking ROCE from 17% to 40% and fixed-asset turnover from 1.99x to 5.10x, with no debt at any point and no equity issued. [F] (NUMBERS) [E] The two durable sources of that performance are verifiable: a regulatory-capability franchise that redesigned an entire product range for CPCB IV+ while smaller competitors had to fund the same transition, and a distribution business at Rs 3,278 crore with 480+ touchpoints, 877,569 service orders and a 90% Net Promoter Score that compounds mechanically off a growing installed base. [F] (AR2026 p.33) (AR2026 p.18) (CALL Jun 2026)

On top of that sits a genuinely new demand pool. Data centres went from 23% to 40% of quarterly power-generation revenue in a year, customers are asking for deliveries to be brought forward rather than deferred, inquiry conversations now extend two years out, and CIL's competitive position in the segment - pre-tender site engineering, lead-time management, 99.99% uptime service - is the kind of incumbency that price-led entrants do not dislodge. [F] [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) The balance sheet gives complete freedom: Rs 3,925 crore of liquid assets, nil debt, 258x interest cover, capex at 2% of sales, 70-75% utilisation and a 77% payout. [F] (AR2026 p.274) (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) Governance is diligent, the audit is clean, the parent has not extracted value through anything exotic, and the promoter has not sold a share in three years. [F] (AR2026 p.41) (NUMBERS)

Every version of our valuation model says the same thing: the price is multiples of the fair value the model can support. Bear Rs 448.9, base Rs 757.6, bull Rs 1,039.7, widest sensitivity cell Rs 996, against Rs 5,100. [F] (NUMBERS) The model is harsh in specific, identifiable ways - a 15% cost of equity for a debt-free 40%-ROCE business, an equity bridge that ignores Rs 3,925 crore of cash, an EBITDA-only cash flow that excludes Rs 783.62 crore of other and equity-accounted income, and a five-year window on a multi-decade annuity. [F] (AR2026 p.274) (AR2026 p.276) [AI] Correcting all of them would not close the gap. [AI]

And the operating case has already begun to wobble in exactly the places this report has documented. Trailing twelve-month EBITDA is marginally below FY26 on 4.3% higher sales; trailing EPS is flat; Q1 FY27 delivered 0.8% profit growth on 17.9% revenue growth at an 18% margin; three unnamed customers are now 31% of revenue; ex-data-centre power generation is growing in the low single digits; domestic industrial fell 1% in FY26; exports are flat; cash conversion is 0.73x; net charges from the parent group doubled to 3.72% of revenue; contingent liabilities trebled; and the Managing Director who delivered the transformation is leaving without a named successor. [F] (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.340) (CALL Aug 2026) (AR2026 p.245) (AR2026 p.324) [E] [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) None of those is fatal. All of them are unpriced at 59.7x trailing earnings. [AI]

subsections.title: What the market may be missing, in both directions

items: **Missing on the bull side - the aftermarket is worth more than the market model implies, and it is not being valued as an annuity.** Every genset installed generates parts and service revenue for fifteen to twenty years; the CPCB IV+ fleet that transitioned from July 2023 to July 2024 starts leaving warranty through FY27; management has never sized this and no analyst has forced it to. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) [AI] A five-year DCF structurally cannot capture it, and neither can a price-to-earnings multiple on a year in which the annuity has barely begun. [AI]

**Missing on the bull side - a third of the balance sheet is invisible in the valuation debate.** Rs 3,925 crore of cash and liquid investments, Rs 602.09 crore of stakes in two businesses growing 28% and 16%, and investment property with a Rs 1,485.52 crore fair value carried at Rs 906.68 crore. [F] (AR2026 p.274) (AR2026 p.30) (AR2026 p.216) None of it is in our model's per-share output. [AI]

**Missing on the bear side - the data-centre revenue has no disclosed contract behind it.** No customer is named, no order value is disclosed, no backlog exists, market share is unknown to management, and the annual report itself warns of 'variability aligned with timing of large project executions'. [F] (AR2026 p.340) (AR2026 p.51) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) The market is capitalising a call-transcript percentage. [AI]

**Missing on the bear side - the economics of the parent relationship are being re-priced against minorities and almost nobody has noticed.** Net non-goods charges from the group went from Rs 185.34 crore to Rs 451.74 crore, 1.78% to 3.72% of revenue, an increase equal to 8.6% of pre-tax profit; the only explanation offered covered the smallest component. [E] (AR2026 p.245) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) Combined with a cost-plus-11% cap on intra-group sales and an FY27 authorisation that would nearly double sales to the UK arm, this is a structural margin question, not a one-year item. [F] (AR2026 p.401) (AR2026 p.398) [AI]

**Missing on both sides - the ex-data-centre business is the real debate, and it is barely discussed.** If non-data-centre power generation, industrial and exports were growing at 12-15%, the data-centre concentration would be an accelerant on a healthy base. On FY26 and Q1 FY27 evidence they are growing at roughly nothing. [E] (CALL Jun 2026) (CALL Aug 2026) Whether that is a tender-cycle trough (management's view) or the true underlying rate is the single most valuable question an investor in this name can answer. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) [AI]

items: **The good five years.** Indian data-centre construction accelerates toward the pace management says it has not yet reached, 78-litre volumes justify Indian localisation, the CPCB IV+ aftermarket annuity arrives and pushes distribution past 30% of sales, rail and marine convert their order intake, defence platforms order, margin re-establishes above 20%, and revenue roughly doubles - the base case's Rs 23,308 crore by year five, or the bull case's Rs 29,874 crore. [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) (CALL Aug 2026) In that world the business is worth far more than today, and the shares may still not be, depending entirely on what multiple survives. [AI]

**The middling five years.** Data centres grow but lumpily, the domestic genset price war caps margin at 19-20%, industrial recovers to mid-single-digit growth, exports stay range-bound, parent charges settle at 3.5-4% of revenue, and revenue compounds at low-teens rates with earnings compounding slightly slower. [AI] This is the base case, and it is a perfectly good business outcome that is nonetheless a poor share outcome at 59.7x. [F] (NUMBERS) [AI]

**The bad five years.** An Indian data-centre capital-expenditure pause of the kind that has periodically hit global AI infrastructure meets a domestic price war and a commodity cycle; three customers become two; power generation posts a -16% quarter more than once; margin reverts to 16-17% as in FY22 and FY23; industrial stays flat; and revenue grows at 5-6%. [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) That is the bear case, and its Rs 448.9 per share is the number that should anchor an investor's sense of downside. [F] (NUMBERS) [AI]

**The tail nobody models.** The parent restructures the India footprint - more manufacturing into Cummins Technologies India, more of the export book at cost-plus-11%, a higher technology charge. [F] (AR2026 p.401) (AR2026 p.398) None of this requires bad faith; it requires only ordinary group-optimisation decisions taken by people who sit on both boards. [AI] It would show up in CIL's numbers as a slow, unexplained margin drift, which is exactly what this report has documented one year of. [E] [AI]

**What is almost certainly not in the possibility space:** financial distress (nil debt, Rs 3,925 crore of liquidity), dilution (no option scheme, no convertible, no issue), or an accounting blow-up (clean audit, no goodwill, no related-party loans, bank returns agreeing with books). [F] (AR2026 p.274) (AR2026 p.77) (AR2026 p.184) This is a low-risk business at a high-risk price. [AI]

sections.title: Research view

subsections.title: Where the price sits, and what drives the gap

blocks.text: At Rs 5,100 the shares trade 91.2% above our bear-case fair value of Rs 448.9, 85.1% above the base case of Rs 757.6 and 79.6% above the bull case of Rs 1,039.7; the widest cell of the discount-rate and terminal-growth grid reaches Rs 996, and the reverse DCF puts the required five-year sales growth at 78.1% against a 13.0% base-case equivalent. [F] (NUMBERS) We issue no rating and no price target, and we do not treat Rs 757.6 as a target - the model's structure is unsuited to this asset in four identifiable ways, and correcting each of them would raise the output. [AI]

**What drives the gap, in order of contribution.** First, model structure: a five-year explicit period with a Gordon terminal value at a 15% cost of equity cannot express a multi-decade installed-base annuity, and 72% of the base-case enterprise value already sits in the terminal value. [E] (NUMBERS) Second, an equity bridge that deducts Rs 37 crore of borrowings and ignores Rs 3,925 crore of cash and liquid investments, Rs 602.09 crore of joint-venture and associate stakes and Rs 1,485.52 crore of investment-property fair value. [F] (AR2026 p.274) (AR2026 p.216) Third, an EBITDA-based free cash flow that excludes Rs 783.62 crore of other and equity-accounted income. [E] (AR2026 p.276) (AR2026 p.318) Fourth, and this one runs the other way: **the market is paying 59.7x trailing earnings on earnings that have stopped growing** - trailing EBITDA of Rs 2,588 crore is marginally below FY26's Rs 2,595 crore on 4.3% higher sales, and trailing EPS of Rs 85.39 is flat against Rs 85.20. [F] (NUMBERS) [E] Some of the gap is model artefact; some of it is a market paying for duration and scarcity that no cash-flow model at this discount rate can validate. Both readings are in the evidence, and we decline to resolve them with a single number. [AI]

items: **This is not a one-to-two-quarter proposition in either direction.** The Q2 FY27 margin print will settle whether the 18% quarter was absorption or a new base, but it will not settle the valuation question, which depends on whether high-teens compounding persists for a decade. [AI]

**The minimum coherent horizon for a long position is three to five years**, because that is how long it takes for the two durable legs - the CPCB IV+ aftermarket annuity and data-centre installed-base service revenue - to show up in the numbers, and it is also how long it takes for the node-migration question to resolve. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) (CALL Jun 2026) [AI]

**The relevant risk over that horizon is de-rating, not impairment.** With nil debt, Rs 3,925 crore of liquidity, no dilution machinery and a clean audit, the downside is a multiple compression on a business that keeps earning 30%+ returns on equity - not a loss of capital through financial failure. [F] (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.274) [AI]
**Position sizing should reflect that three unnamed customers supply 31% of revenue** and that the disclosure needed to monitor them does not exist. [F] (AR2026 p.340) [AI]

**For an investor already long**, the operating evidence in FY26 and Q1 FY27 does not mandate action; the valuation evidence means there is no margin of safety for any of the documented risks. [AI] **For an investor not long**, nothing in these documents makes Rs 5,100 defensible on cash flow, and the honest position is that this is a quality-versus-price problem with no analytical resolution short of a lower price or materially better disclosure. [AI]

**Q2 FY27 results, due by the second week of November 2026** - the first print containing the Q2 price increase and the first test of whether the 18% operating margin reverses. Re-review regardless of outcome. [F] (AR2026 p.87) [AI]

**Q3 FY27 results, due by the second week of February 2027** - by then three quarters of FY27 distribution growth will show whether the 14% quarter was availability-driven, and the CPCB IV+ warranty-expiry annuity should be visible. [F] (AR2026 p.87) [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)

**Q4 and FY27 results, due by the fourth week of May 2027, and the FY27 annual report** - the only place the three-customer concentration figure, the full-year related-party schedule, the FY28 related-party caps and the contingent-liability position are disclosed. These four disclosures matter more than any three quarterly prints. [F] (AR2026 p.87) (AR2026 p.340) (AR2026 p.394) (AR2026 p.324) [AI]
**On any announcement naming a successor to the Managing Director**, or any further change in the Chief Financial Officer. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)
**On any order-book, installed-capacity, market-share or segment-margin disclosure**, because each would materially change what can be analysed in this name. [F] [AI]
**On any adverse order in the Rs 229.74 crore GST matter, or disclosure on the whistle-blower investigations.** [F] (AR2026 p.187) (AR2026 p.188)
**On a 78-litre localisation decision, or a first battery-energy-storage order**, both of which have been pending for four quarters or more. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

**On a share price below roughly the 52-week low of Rs 3,803**, at which point the gap to the model's bull case narrows enough that the quality-versus-price problem becomes a different conversation. [F] (NUMBERS) [AI]

sections.title: Initial coverage

blocks.text: **This is initial coverage.** No previous quarterly report exists in the evidence base, so there is no prior set of numbers, disclosures, guidance items, risks or thesis statements to compare against. [F] The only earlier material available is this dashboard's own research notes, which describe the business as an installed-base and emissions-compliance franchise with cyclical demand exposure, parent control over technology and transfer pricing, and a multiple that 'leaves little room for a cyclical downturn' at 58x - and which explicitly label the moat argument as 'a reasoned view from public industry structure, not a claim verified against an external source in this pass'. [BOARD] Our work in the FY26 annual report and the four earnings-call transcripts supports each of those propositions and adds four findings the notes did not contain: the three-customer concentration of about 31% of revenue disclosed only in the consolidated segment note; the doubling of net non-goods charges from the parent group from 1.78% to 3.72% of revenue; the trebling of contingent liabilities driven by a Rs 229.74 crore GST matter; and the Q1 FY27 margin compression to 18% with profit growth of 0.8% on revenue growth of 17.9%. [F] (AR2026 p.340) (AR2026 p.245) (AR2026 p.324) (NUMBERS) [E] From the next quarter, the guidance tracker in this report becomes the baseline against which management's FY27 statements should be tested, and the monitoring dashboard sets out the twelve metrics we will roll forward. [AI]
