summary.one_line: Cummins India is a debt-free, 40%-ROCE engine and genset franchise whose FY26 record was genuine but whose growth has narrowed onto data centres and three unnamed customers, whose margin has already turned down in Q1 FY27, and whose Rs 5,100 share price sits far above every fair value our DCF model can support.
bull_points: The aftermarket annuity is the real quality: distribution revenue of Rs 3,278 crore in FY26, +22% and 27.4% of net sales, off 480+ 4S touchpoints, 110+ retail touchpoints, 877,569 service orders and a 90% Net Promoter Score described as the highest ever achieved globally in the Cummins group, with growth explicitly not price-led. [F] (AR2026 p.18) (AR2026 p.10) (CALL Jun 2026) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

Data centres have become the dominant marginal buyer of Indian high-horsepower gensets and CIL is the incumbent: data centres rose from 23% to 40% of quarterly power-generation revenue in a year, domestic power generation grew 35% to Rs 1,424 crore in Q1 FY27, and customers are asking for deliveries to be brought forward rather than deferred. [F] [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Emission-norm capability is a recurring barrier that smaller competitors must fund repeatedly: the entire sub-800 kW range was redesigned for CPCB IV+, retrofit emission device approvals were obtained for CPCB I and II engines, and Euro Stage V, Tier III, Stage IIIA, CEV BS V and FM/UL certifications were added in FY26 on own R&D of only Rs 10.54 crore, 0.09% of sales. [F] (AR2026 p.33) (AR2026 p.34)

Growth needs almost no capital: capex was Rs 247 crore or 2.0% of sales, utilisation is 70-75% with 'no major capital expenditure plan', and FY21-FY26 delivered Rs 7,783 crore of incremental sales on roughly Rs 832 crore of cumulative capex, taking ROCE from 17% to 40% and fixed-asset turnover from 1.99x to 5.10x. [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) (CALL Jun 2026) [E]

The balance sheet removes financial risk entirely: nil borrowings, 258x interest cover, a 3.32 current ratio, Rs 3,925 crore of cash, bank deposits and liquid investments (34.7% of assets) against Rs 150.66 crore of capital commitments, no guarantees, no related-party loans, no dilution machinery and a 77% dividend payout. [F] (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.274) (AR2026 p.235) (AR2026 p.255) [E]
bear_points: The price sits far outside every scenario our model can construct: bear Rs 448.9, base Rs 757.6 and bull Rs 1,039.7 per share against Rs 5,100, with the widest cell of the WACC and terminal-growth grid reaching only Rs 996 and the reverse DCF implying a 78.1% five-year sales CAGR against a 13.0% base-case equivalent - flagged red by our model's own screen. [F] (NUMBERS) [E]

Growth has concentrated into one lumpy end-market and three unnamed customers: sales of about Rs 3,734.71 crore came from three external customers in FY26 against Rs 2,226.78 crore from two in FY25, roughly 30.8% of consolidated revenue versus 21.4%, disclosed only in a segment footnote and never mentioned on any earnings call. [F] (AR2026 p.340) [E] Ex-data-centre power generation grew in the low single digits in Q1 FY27, domestic industrial fell 1% in FY26 and exports were flat. [E] (CALL Aug 2026) (CALL Jun 2026)

Earnings have stopped growing and margin has turned: Q1 FY27 operating margin was 18% against 21-22% in each of the prior four quarters, PAT rose 0.8% on sales up 17.9%, trailing EBITDA of Rs 2,588 crore is marginally below FY26's Rs 2,595 crore on 4.3% higher sales, and trailing EPS of Rs 85.39 is flat against Rs 85.20 - while the stock trades at 59.7x trailing earnings. [F] (NUMBERS) No price increase was taken in Q1, one followed in Q2 with realisation lagging 'at least a quarter', and management conceded recovery would be incomplete. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Value is being re-priced toward the parent: net non-goods charges from the group - royalty, support services and net reimbursements - more than doubled from Rs 185.34 crore to Rs 451.74 crore, from 1.78% to 3.72% of revenue, an increase equal to 8.6% of pre-tax profit, with an explanation offered only for the smallest component. [E] (AR2026 p.245) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) FY27 related-party caps total Rs 10,591 crore, about 87% of FY26 consolidated turnover, priced on internally tested cost-plus formulas with no external valuation report.
